title: [sim/crit] MessageConverter: MigrationProtocolMessages absent from converter switch — IAE/drop on 2PC wire path (RDR-004 class)
description: sim:von/MessageConverter.java:48-101. 6 Prepare/Commit/Abort subtypes are sealed-permitted but unhandled; default throws IAE; 2PC over Transport dies. Fix: add converter+handler cases.
design:
### MigrationProtocolMessages silently crash/drop on wire path (RDR-004 class)
- Location (verifier-confirmed): **sim:von/MessageConverter.java:48-101**
- Root cause: MigrationProtocolMessages (PrepareRequest, PrepareResponse, CommitRequest, CommitResponse, AbortRequest, AbortResponse) are permitted subtypes of Message.sealed (Message.java:55) but are absent from MessageConverter.toTransport()'s switch. The default branch throws IllegalArgumentException. On the receiver side, Bubble.handleMessage() (Bubble.java:422-432) has no case for MigrationProtocolMessages and falls to 'default -> log.warn(...)' — the message is silently discarded. The entire 2PC migration protocol is inoperative when messages pass through SocketTransport serialization. This is the same silent-data-loss class as RDR-004 D3.
- Fix: Add converter cases for all six MigrationProtocolMessages subtypes in MessageConverter.toTransport/fromTransport. Add a handler case in Bubble.handleMessage that routes 2PC messages to the appropriate coordinator. Add a round-trip serialization test covering every MigrationProtocolMessages subtype.
- Verifier evidence: Independently confirmed. Message.java:52-55 shows `sealed interface Message permits ... MigrationProtocolMessages`. MessageConverter.java:49-68 switches on message type with cases only for GhostSync, JoinRequest, JoinResponse, Move, Leave, Ack, Query, QueryResponse — no case for MigrationProtocolMessages or any of its subtypes. The default branch at line 67 throws `IllegalArgumentException("Unknown Message type: ...")`. Any attempt to serialize a migration 2PC message through SocketTransport wil

**Test pointer**: Test: each Prepare/Commit/Abort request+response round-trips via MessageConverter.

**Build/verify**: `mvn test -pl simulation -Dtest=<NewTest> -Dsurefire.rerunFailingTestsCount=0` (assertions ON).
acceptance_criteria: MessageConverter.toTransport/fromTransport handle all six MigrationProtocolMessages subtypes and Bubble.handleMessage routes them; a 2PC message round-trips through Transport without IllegalArgumentException.
close_reason: MessageConverter to/fromTransport handle all 6 MigrationProtocolMessages via primitive-only TransportMigrationMessage (rich IdempotencyToken/EntitySnapshot decomposed, NOT on wire); VonTransportFilter allow-list kept narrow; Bubble.handleMessage routes 2PC to migrationHandler. Regression MigrationProtocol2PCWireRoundTripTest (round-trip+narrow-filter-survival+reject-non-wire) + BubbleMigrationRoutingTest. RDR-004 hygiene satisfied. Green.

title: [sim/crit] BubbleGhostManager.handleGhostBatch: incoming ghost lifecycle.onCreate never called — onUpdate computeIfPresent is a no-op for all received ghosts
description: sim:ghost/BubbleGhostManager.java:252-255. Receiver-side staleness tracking never functions. Fix: onCreate if state==null before onUpdate.
design:
### BubbleGhostManager.handleGhostBatch — incoming ghost lifecycle state never created, onUpdate is always a no-op
- Location (verifier-confirmed): **sim:ghost/BubbleGhostManager.java:252-254**
- Root cause: handleGhostBatch() calls `lifecycle.onUpdate(ghost.entityId().toDebugString(), ghost.timestamp())` for each received ghost. GhostLifecycleStateMachine.onUpdate() uses `states.computeIfPresent()` — if no entry for that entityId exists, it silently no-ops and returns null. For incoming (received) ghosts, lifecycle.onCreate() is never called, so no entry is ever created. Every lifecycle.onUpdate() call in the receive path is therefore a guaranteed no-op. Ghost staleness tracking for the receiving side is completely non-functional: all received ghosts have no lifecycle state, and expireStaleGhosts() will never expire them.
- Fix: In handleGhostBatch, call `lifecycle.onCreate(entityId, fromBubbleId, timestamp)` before onUpdate if the entity is new. Pattern: `if (lifecycle.getState(entityId) == null) { lifecycle.onCreate(entityId, fromBubbleId, ghost.timestamp()); } lifecycle.onUpdate(entityId, ghost.timestamp());`
- Verifier evidence: Inspected BubbleGhostManager.java lines 252-255 and GhostLifecycleStateMachine.java lines 234-237. handleGhostBatch() calls only lifecycle.onUpdate() for each received ghost; lifecycle.onCreate() is never called in that path. GhostLifecycleStateMachine.onUpdate() uses states.computeIfPresent(entityId, ...) (line 237), which returns null and does nothing when the key is absent. Since onCreate() (which does states.put(), line 219) is never called for incoming ghosts, computeIfPresent will always f

### BubbleGhostManager: incoming ghost lifecycle.onCreate never called — onUpdate is a no-op for all received ghosts
- Location (verifier-confirmed): **sim:ghost/BubbleGhostManager.java:253-255**
- Root cause: handleGhostBatch() at line 254 calls `lifecycle.onUpdate(ghost.entityId().toDebugString(), ghost.timestamp())` for each received ghost. GhostLifecycleStateMachine.onUpdate() is implemented with computeIfPresent(), which is a no-op when the key is absent. lifecycle.onCreate() is only called in notifyEntityNearBoundary() (line 196), which is the sender path. On the receiver side, onCreate() is never called. Therefore every lifecycle.onUpdate() call in handleGhostBatch() silently does nothing: the lifecycle state machine tracks zero state for any received ghost. Staleness detection, TTL expiry, and the CREATED→ACTIVE state transition are all non-functional for received ghosts.
- Fix: In handleGhostBatch(), before calling lifecycle.onUpdate(), check if the entity is already registered and call onCreate() if not: if (lifecycle.getState(ghost.entityId().toDebugString()) == null) { lifecycle.onCreate(ghost.entityId().toDebugString(), fromBubbleId, ghost.timestamp()); }
- Verifier evidence: Confirmed by direct inspection. `BubbleGhostManager.handleGhostBatch()` (lines 253-255) calls `lifecycle.onUpdate(ghost.entityId().toDebugString(), ghost.timestamp())` for every received ghost. `GhostLifecycleStateMachine.onUpdate()` (lines 237-251) uses `states.computeIfPresent(entityId, ...)` — a no-op when the key is absent. `lifecycle.onCreate()` is called only at line 196, inside `notifyEntityNearBoundary()`, which is the local sender path. On the receiver side there is no `onCreate()` call

**Test pointer**: Test: receiver lifecycle state advances across ghost batches.

**Build/verify**: `mvn test -pl simulation -Dtest=<NewTest> -Dsurefire.rerunFailingTestsCount=0` (assertions ON).
acceptance_criteria: handleGhostBatch registers the lifecycle (onCreate) for a previously-unseen incoming ghost before onUpdate, so receiver-side staleness tracking actually advances; a test sends two batches for one ghost and asserts the lifecycle state/timestamp updated.
close_reason: handleGhostBatch now onCreate()s a previously-unseen incoming ghost before onUpdate() (computeIfPresent was a no-op without prior state). Added getLifecycleStateForTesting seam. BubbleGhostManagerTest.testHandleGhostBatchRegistersReceiverLifecycle green.

title: [sim/crit] P2PGhostChannel.fromTransportGhost reconstructs ID as private StringEntityID — ClassCastException at use site
description: sim:ghost/P2PGhostChannel.java:349-350. Unchecked cast compiles via erasure; any handler type-checking entityId fails on every deserialized cross-bubble ghost. Fix: register EntityID deserializer/factory at construction.
design:
### P2PGhostChannel — entity ID type always reconstructed as private StringEntityID, causing ClassCastException
- Location (verifier-confirmed): **sim:ghost/P2PGhostChannel.java:349-350**
- Root cause: fromTransportGhost() reconstructs the entity ID as `(ID) new StringEntityID(tg.entityId())` where StringEntityID is a private record inside P2PGhostChannel. The unchecked cast compiles and succeeds at runtime due to type erasure. However, any downstream handler that type-checks the ghost's entityId (e.g., `(ConcreteEntityID) ghost.entityId()`, `instanceof`, or equality via CompareTo across types) will receive a runtime ClassCastException or incorrect behavior for every ghost received over the P2P channel. This is a RDR-004 class silent-data-corruption: the ghost is delivered but with a fundamentally wrong ID type, silently breaking all callers that rely on the concrete ID type.
- Fix: The channel needs an EntityID deserializer registered at construction time (matching the sender's ID type), or the EntityID must be reconstructable from its debug string via a factory. Add a `Function<String, ID> idFactory` constructor parameter and use it in fromTransportGhost. For the specific case where ID is the project's StringEntityID (not the private one), the caller can supply `StringEntityID::new`. For other ID types, the factory must be provided.
- Verifier evidence: Confirmed. P2PGhostChannel.java line 350 constructs the ghost entity ID as `(ID) new StringEntityID(tg.entityId())` where `StringEntityID` is a private record inside `P2PGhostChannel` (completely separate from the public `com.hellblazer.luciferase.simulation.entity.StringEntityID`). 

GhostStateListener.java line 154 then does `(StringEntityID) entityId` — importing `com.hellblazer.luciferase.simulation.entity.StringEntityID`. Because the runtime type is `P2PGhostChannel$StringEntityID` (a disti

### P2PGhostChannel: ID type erasure — unchecked cast to caller's ID type produces ClassCastException at use site
- Location (verifier-confirmed): **sim:ghost/P2PGhostChannel.java:349-351**
- Root cause: fromTransportGhost() always reconstructs the entity ID as `(ID) new StringEntityID(tg.entityId())`. The @SuppressWarnings("unchecked") suppresses the compiler's warning. If the P2PGhostChannel is instantiated with any ID type other than StringEntityID (e.g., a UUIDEntityID, IntEntityID, or the project's own EntityID subclass), downstream code that reads the entityId() and casts it to the actual type will get a ClassCastException. This is an RDR-004 class silent-failure: the ghost is accepted and processed with a wrong ID type, and the error surfaces only when the ID is actually used.
- Fix: Require callers to provide an EntityID deserializer/factory via the constructor or a separate interface, e.g., `Function<String, ID> entityIdDeserializer`. Use it in fromTransportGhost() instead of the hardcoded StringEntityID cast.
- Verifier evidence: Line 350 of P2PGhostChannel.java: `(ID) new StringEntityID(tg.entityId())` is a type-unsafe cast suppressed with @SuppressWarnings("unchecked"). The class is declared `P2PGhostChannel<ID extends EntityID, Content>` with no bound restricting ID to StringEntityID. Every current instantiation in the codebase happens to use `StringEntityID` (ClusterIntegrationTest.java:559, BubbleGhostManagerP2PIntegrationTest.java:97-98, P2PGhostChannelTest.java:89-90), so no ClassCastException fires today. However

**Test pointer**: Test: deserialize ghost, assert entityId instanceof real ID type and equals original.

**Build/verify**: `mvn test -pl simulation -Dtest=<NewTest> -Dsurefire.rerunFailingTestsCount=0` (assertions ON).
acceptance_criteria: P2PGhostChannel reconstructs the real EntityID type via an injected deserializer/factory matching the sender; a cross-bubble ghost round-trip yields an entityId of the caller's ID type usable by handlers (no ClassCastException).
close_reason: P2PGhostChannel now reconstructs the caller's real EntityID via an injected Function<String,ID> idFactory (new ctor); default ctor inverts StringEntityID.toDebugString. Removed private placeholder StringEntityID record. P2PGhostChannelTest.testReceivedGhostEntityIdIsRealTypeAndEqualsOriginal green.

title: ESVT GPU kernel far-pointer protocol mismatch: kernel reads in-band, builder/CPU use separate farPointers[] (never uploaded)
description: PRE-EXISTING (surfaced during Luciferase-yhue6 review). The ESVT far-pointer encodings differ between CPU and GPU: ESVTBuilder stores far-pointer VALUES in a separate int[] farPointers array; CPU traversal (ESVTData.resolveChildPtr / ESVTNodeUnified.getChildIndex) resolves via farPointers[index]. But the GPU kernel render/src/main/resources/kernels/esvt_ray_traversal.cl getChildIndex (~line 192) resolves far by reading nodes[parentIdx + childPtr].childDescriptor IN-BAND from the node array, and ESVTOpenCLRenderer.uploadDataBuffers uploads only nodes+contours — no farPointers buffer, and the kernel signature has no such arg. So when GPU rendering a model with far pointers (e.g. the Stanford Bunny: 22 far pointers in a 163k-node tree), far-flagged nodes resolve to wrong child indices -> silently corrupt geometry for rays through those nodes (not a crash). Independent of yhue6 (CPU build/layout): yhue6 fixed the CPU build overflow and REDUCED far pointers; this is the GPU-side resolution protocol. Fix options: (a) builder emits in-band sentinel far nodes matching the kernel, or (b) add a __global const int* farPointers buffer to the kernel + ESVTOpenCLRenderer + setKernelArguments and resolve from it (matching CPU). Either way add a build-time far-count guard and re-enable/extend ESVTGPUCPUParityTest (currently gated behind RUN_GPU_TESTS) to cover a far-pointer model. NOTE: GPU rendering is opt-in (toggle); the default CPU/entity render path the bunny demo uses is unaffected.
acceptance_criteria: GPU ESVT render of a far-pointer model (e.g. bunny) matches CPU traversal (parity test with far pointers passes); far-pointer encoding is consistent between builder, CPU traversal, and GPU kernel; build-time far-count guard present.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #232 (merged 74850f43). All acceptance criteria met: encoding consistent across builder/CPU/OpenCL/GLSL; far-count guard present (pre-existing, yhue6); parity test with far-pointer model added (GPU-gated; headless non-zero-index CPU resolution test pins the protocol in CI). CI green first pass. Follow-up filed: Luciferase-vkl96 (pre-existing DynamicKernelSelectionTest local JVM crash).

title: ESVTBuilder far-pointer overflow: BFS node layout exhausts the 15-bit far-index (bunny can't render)
description: ESVTBuilder.createNodes (render/.../esvt/builder/ESVTBuilder.java ~745-758) lays out nodes in BFS order, so a parent's children sit tens-of-thousands of slots ahead -> relativeOffset > MAX_CHILD_PTR (32767) for most internal nodes -> a far pointer is allocated for nearly every node. The far-pointer INDEX is itself stored in the same 15-bit child-ptr field via setChildPtr(farIndex), so once >32767 far pointers exist it throws 'Child pointer must fit in 15 bits (max 32767), got: 32768'. Net: ESVT cannot build any model large enough to need >32767 far pointers. The Stanford Bunny (47705 voxels) is the first demo asset to hit it -> /api/render/create (ESVT) returns 400 -> render.html shows a stale earlier (sphere) render. Fix: re-order the node array to a parent-then-children-block (DFS/page) layout so relativeOffset stays small and far pointers become rare, recomputing pointers from the new layout (CPU/GPU traversal already follows relative+far pointers, so layout-agnostic). Acceptance: build ESVT from the 47705-voxel bunny succeeds; far-pointer count ~0; bunny renders. Discovered via headless portal validation 2026-06-03.
acceptance_criteria: ESVT build from the Stanford Bunny (47705 voxels, depth 8) succeeds (no child-ptr overflow); far-pointer count is small/zero; /api/render/create ESVT returns 200; regression test covers it.
close_reason: Child-contiguous ESVT node layout replaces BFS, keeping child-pointer offsets subtree-local so far pointers are rare (22 on a 64k-voxel block, was >32767 -> 15-bit overflow). Stanford Bunny now builds (163,448 nodes) and renders end-to-end via render.html ESVT (was 400). Added fail-loud far-index guard, corrected stale comments, regression test (builds without overflow + far-count sane; fails on old code). Traversal correctness preserved (same childMask+relative/far pointer contract; maintained esvt.traversal/core suites green with the new layout). Stacked review (code-review-expert + substantive-critic) done; the GPU far-pointer protocol mismatch they surfaced is pre-existing and tracked separately. Branch feature/yhue6-esvt-far-pointer-layout (off main), unpushed.

title: [CRIT] balancing/fault PartitionRecovery implementations are hollow stubs shipped as production

title: tkvb regression: simulation tests fabricate TetreeKeys from magic constants that decode to pyramid types 6/7 under new layout
description: DETERMINISTIC tkvb regression (NOT a flake — my earlier flake diagnosis was wrong; local green runs used a stale ~/.m2 lucien jar). 5 tests fail: BubbleBoundsTest.testFromTetreeKeyLevel10 (0x123456&0x3F=type6), testOverlapsDisjoint (0xFFFFFF->type7), TetreeNeighborFinderTest.testNoSelfNeighbor (7L->type7), testNeighborSymmetry (6L->type6), testNeighborStability_RepeatedCalls (15L->type7). # Execution context (nx_enrich_beads, 2026-05-31)

Repo /Users/hal.hildebrand/git/Luciferase · module `lucien` · pkg ...lucien.forest.ghost

NOTE: live class is GhostBoundaryDetector (~line 626 identifyBoundaryElements), NOT ElementGhostManager (dead — see B7/Luciferase-8ggq). Target GBD; factor the descent into one shared method.

## t8code ghost-v3 to port (ref t8_forest_ghost.cxx ~507-634, t8_forest_ghost_search_boundary)
Recursive SFC descent; each level carries owner-rank interval bounds_per_level[level]=[lower,upper] (min/max owning rank over the node's SFC subrange):
1. compute [lower,upper] for the element's SFC descendant range from partition contiguous cut points (owner-of-first-descendant, owner-of-last-descendant).
2. if lower==upper==currentRank → subtree locally owned/interior; if ALL faces owned locally → RETURN EARLY (prune subtree).
3. if subrange spans other ranks → recurse into children, narrowing bounds per child.
4. at leaves: boundary element iff >=1 face neighbor owned by a different rank.
Converts O(N) flat scan → logarithmic-fanout descent pruning owned subtrees.

## 3 sub-tasks
1. subMap range primitive: find the NavigableMap/ConcurrentSkipListMap accessor on the spatial index (near getSpatialKeys() or a package-private map getter) to get subMap(fromKey,true,toKey,true) over an SFC subrange. VERIFY exact accessor name/visibility.
2. owner-of-key from ShapeWeightPartitioner cut points: binary search over SFC-contiguous cut points → O(log P). VERIFY whether an ownerOfKey helper exists or add a thin binary-search wrapper. [lower,upper]=[ownerOf(firstDescendant),ownerOf(lastDescendant)].
3. integration: replace flat-scan loop in identifyBoundaryElements with bounded-descent seeded at SFC root range; preserve return contract (set/collection of boundary keys); dedup vs GBD by factoring one shared method.

title: Phase 0 Step 2.1: Rewrite findWithinRadius to use bounding(Spatial.Sphere)
description:
Step 3 validation (Luciferase-sc4) discovered that SpatialNeighborIndex.findWithinRadius routes range queries through the k-NN cache, producing a 172× REGRESSION vs linear scan at N=100K, r=50 (271ms vs 1.6ms).

Root cause: findWithinRadius delegates to tetree.findNeighborsIncludingGhosts(center, radius) which is implemented as kNearestNeighbors(position, Integer.MAX_VALUE, radius) at AbstractSpatialIndex.java:5096. This routes unbounded-result range queries through a cache keyed on k that stores giant id lists, causing GC pressure and catastrophic per-iteration variance.

Fix: use AbstractSpatialIndex.bounding(Spatial.Sphere) which is the proper range-by-volume primitive (AbstractSpatialIndex.java:209). Post-filter results by Euclidean distance to the centroid.

Sketch:
```java
public List<Node> findWithinRadius(Point3D center, float radius) {
    var sphere = new Spatial.Sphere((float)center.getX(), (float)center.getY(), (float)center.getZ(), radius);
    var centerPt = toPoint3f(center);
    var radiusSq = radius * radius;
    return tetree.bounding(sphere)
        .flatMap(node -> node.entityIds().stream())
        .distinct()
        .map(tetree::getEntity)
        .filter(Objects::nonNull)
        .filter(n -> centerPt.distanceSquared(toPoint3f(n.position())) <= radiusSq)
        .collect(Collectors.toList());
}
```

The bounding(Spatial volume) method uses spatialRangeQuery(bounds, includeIntersecting=true) on the sphere's AABB then filter by doesNodeIntersectVolume which dispatches to Spatial.Sphere.intersects (sphere-AABB intersection at Spatial.java:88-96).

Acceptance:
- findWithinRadius rewritten using bounding(Spatial.Sphere) + radius post-filter
- VoN test suite passes unchanged
- Step 3 JMH re-run shows findWithinRadius @ N=100K r=50 mean <= 5ms (Step 4 stress threshold)
- Step 3 JMH re-run shows sub-linear scaling for findWithinRadius at r=50
- New results persisted as simulation/doc/baselines/simulation-von-aoi-tetree-2026-05.json (overwriting current Step 3 results)
- Step 4 go/no-go decision applied against corrected results

See: docs/rdr/RDR-003-fcc-aligned-spatial-indexing.md §Revision History 2026-05-23 (Phase 0 Step 4 thresholds)
See: simulation/doc/baselines/README.md §Confounds surfaced
See: T2 luciferase/design-rdr-003-phase-0-step-3-validation-results

title: P2.2: Atomic sealed interface migration — aabt record to sealed interface
description:
Phase 2, Atomic migration for RDR-001. Single commit replacing aabt record with sealed interface.

Context:
  RDR: docs/rdr/RDR-001-axis-aligned-bounding-tetrahedra.md (Technical Design section)
  Key files: All files from P2.1 plus Tet.java
  Search keywords: aabt sealed interface Tet implements Spatial containsUltraFast toVolumeBounds

THIS MUST BE A SINGLE ATOMIC COMMIT. The aabt record cannot coexist with the sealed interface.

Changes in one commit:
1. Replace 'record aabt(6 floats) implements Spatial' with:
   sealed interface aabt permits Tet {
     boolean contains(float px, float py, float pz);
     boolean containsTet(Tet other);
     boolean intersectsTet(Tet other);
     float[][] vertices();
     VolumeBounds toVolumeBounds();
   }

2. Tet implements Spatial, aabt:
   - contains() → delegates to containsUltraFast()
   - containsTet() → check all 4 vertices of other via containsUltraFast()
   - intersectsTet() → SAT test via TetrahedralGeometry
   - vertices() → delegates to coordinates() (convert Point3i[] to float[][])
   - toVolumeBounds() → compute AABB from 4 vertices

3. Migrate all 9 callsites (see RDR callsite inventory):
   #1 Cube.containedBy(aabt) → aabt.contains(cornerMin) && aabt.contains(cornerMax)
   #2 Sphere.containedBy(aabt) → face-normal distance test (4 faces)
   #3 Parallelepiped.containedBy(aabt) → aabt.contains() on all 8 corners
   #4 Tetrahedron.containedBy(aabt) → aabt.contains(a/b/c/d)
   #5 aabb.containedBy(aabt) → aabt.contains() on all 8 corners
   #6 aabt.containedBy(aabt) → deleted (was self-referential record)
   #7 BoundingBox.containedBy(aabt) → aabt.toVolumeBounds() then AABB compare
   #8 VolumeBounds.from(): DELETE case Spatial.aabt, ADD case Tet → tet.toVolumeBounds()
   #9 Spatial.default intersects(aabt): rewrite — no more record accessors

4. Fix Simplex.containedBy(aabt) → reconstruct Tet from index, delegate to aabt.containsTet()
5. Fix Simplex.intersects() → reconstruct Tet, delegate to SAT intersection

6. Enable @Disabled tests from P2.1, verify all pass

Note on circularity: Spatial contains nested aabt, aabt permits Tet, Tet implements Spatial, aabt.

title: Fix DensityRegion.bounds immutability for E2E tests
description: E2E integration tests (TetrahedralForestE2ETest) fail because DensityRegion.bounds is final and captured at addTree() time. When tests call expandGlobalBounds() after tree creation, the DensityRegion retains old bounds, breaking volume calculations in considerSubdivision(). Fix options: (1) Refactor tests to set bounds before addTree() [test-only, minimal impact], (2) Make DensityRegion.bounds mutable [API change], (3) Pass bounds to addTree() [API change]. Recommendation: Option 1 (test-only refactoring). Blocks: Luciferase-m1if
design:
## Fix DensityRegion.bounds Immutability

### Problem
TetrahedralForestE2ETest (4 tests) fail because:
1. Test calls addTree() → DensityRegion created with bounds captured at creation
2. Test calls expandGlobalBounds() to grow bounds
3. DensityRegion.bounds is final, retains old (smaller) bounds
4. considerSubdivision() uses stale bounds for volume calculation
5. Subdivision threshold never met, tests fail

### Root Cause
DensityRegion inner class (AdaptiveForest.java) has:
- final TreeBounds assignedRegion (captured at addTree time)
- No mechanism to update bounds after tree creation

### Solution Options

**Option 1 (RECOMMENDED): Refactor tests**
- Set correct bounds BEFORE calling addTree()
- No API changes required
- Test-only modification (minimal impact)
- Files: TetrahedralForestE2ETest.java only

**Option 2: Make DensityRegion.bounds mutable**
- Change final TreeBounds to volatile TreeBounds
- Add updateBounds(TreeBounds) method
- API change affects AdaptiveForest internal contract
- Files: AdaptiveForest.java (DensityRegion inner class)

**Option 3: Pass bounds to addTree()**
- API signature change: addTree(SpatialIndex, TreeMetadata, TreeBounds)
- Breaking change for all callers
- Files: AdaptiveForest.java, all test files calling addTree()

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 4 TetrahedralForestE2ETest tests passing
- [ ] No API breaking changes (if Option 1)
- [ ] No regressions in existing 2411 passing tests
- [ ] Volume calculations use correct (expanded) bounds
- [ ] Subdivision thresholds triggered correctly

### Implementation Steps (Option 1)
1. In each failing test, identify where expandGlobalBounds() is called
2. Move bounds setup BEFORE addTree() call
3. Remove expandGlobalBounds() calls (or keep as no-op verification)
4. Run tests to verify 4/4 passing
5. Run full test suite to verify no regressions

design:
## Java Architecture: Tetrahedral Entity Redistribution (v2)

### Method: redistributeEntitiesTetrahedral()
Unified method handles both 6-child (S0-S5) and 8-child (Bey) cases.
Accepts List of child trees and List of child Tets.

### Algorithm
1. For each entity in parentRegion.entityPositions:
   a. Primary: iterate children in index order
      - Call childTets.get(i).containsUltraFast(px, py, pz)
      - First match wins (lowest index = deterministic tie-break)
      - break on first match
   b. Fallback (no tet contains point - FP edge case):
      - Compute centroid of each child tet: (v0+v1+v2+v3)/4
      - Assign to nearest centroid (squared distance, skip sqrt)
      - Increment fallbackCount for logging
2. Remove entity from parent spatial index
3. Insert into child spatial index
4. Update density tracking via trackEntityInsertion()

### Key Properties
- Uses Tet.containsUltraFast() exclusively (NOT AABB containsPoint)
- Centroid = tetrahedral centroid (NOT cube center formula)
- First-match-wins is deterministic (iteration order is index order)
- No entity loss: every entity assigned somewhere
- Logging: total redistributed + fallback count

### Concurrency
- parentRegion.entityPositions is ConcurrentHashMap (safe iteration)
- parentIndex.removeEntity and childIndex.insert are thread-safe
- trackEntityInsertion uses AtomicInteger increments
- No synchronized blocks

### Edge Cases
- Entity on tet face/edge: first containing tet wins
- Entity outside all tets (FP rounding): nearest centroid fallback
- Empty parent: no-op with debug log
- Single entity: full assignment logic

### Acceptance Criteria
- All entities redistributed (zero entity loss)
- Uses Tet.containsUltraFast, NOT AABB
- Boundary entities assigned to lowest-index child
- Centroid fallback uses tetrahedral centroid
- Entity count in children sums to parent count
- Density tracking updated for all children
- Works for both 6-child and 8-child cases

## Java Architecture: Dual-Path subdivideTetrahedral() (v2 corrected)

### Classes to Modify
AdaptiveForest.java (lucien/src/main/java/.../forest/AdaptiveForest.java)

### CRITICAL: Dual-Dispatch via Pattern Matching on TreeBounds

The method dispatches on the PARENT TreeBounds type using Java 24 pattern matching:
- CubicBounds parent -> 6 S0-S5 children (cube-to-tet tiling)
- TetrahedralBounds parent -> 8 Bey children (tet-to-tet refinement)

### Main Dispatcher
subdivideTetrahedral() uses CAS guard (tryMarkSubdivided), then pattern-matches:
  case CubicBounds cubic -> subdivideCubeToTets()
  case TetrahedralBounds tetBounds -> subdivideTetToTets()
  case null -> fallback to octant

### Case A: subdivideCubeToTets -- 6 S0-S5 Children
1. Validate non-negative coordinates (fallback to octant if negative)
2. Compute level via tetLevelFromEdgeLength() (fallback if not power-of-2)
3. Validate grid alignment (fallback if misaligned)
4. Create 6 Tet(anchor, level, type) for types 0-5
5. Wrap each in TetrahedralBounds (NOT AABB)
6. Create child trees via createChildTreeWithBounds()
7. Redistribute entities, remove parent (Phase 1)

### Case B: subdivideTetToTets -- 8 Bey Children
1. Check max refinement level
2. BeySubdivision.subdivide(parentTet) -> Tet[8]
3. Wrap each in TetrahedralBounds
4. Create child trees via createChildTreeWithBounds()
5. Redistribute entities, remove parent (Phase 1)

### Helper: tetLevelFromEdgeLength()
Returns -1 if edge not power-of-2 or out of range.

### CRITICAL GEOMETRIC RULES
- S0-S5 (6 children) ONLY for CUBIC parent
- Bey (8 children) ONLY for TETRAHEDRAL parent
- Children ALWAYS get TetrahedralBounds(tet), NEVER AABB
- CAS guard prevents concurrent double-subdivision

### Acceptance Criteria
- CubicBounds parent produces exactly 6 children
- TetrahedralBounds parent produces exactly 8 children
- Children store TetrahedralBounds(tet), NOT EntityBounds
- Negative/non-power-of-2/misaligned coords fall back to octant
- CAS guard prevents double subdivision
- Pattern matching switch on TreeBounds (Java 24)

title: Add comprehensive thread-safety contract documentation
description: Class javadoc says 'Thread-safe' but doesn't specify constraints: components must not call back, must publish state properly, callers must not unregister while another thread starts same component. False confidence leads to unsafe code. Solution: Add Thread-Safety section to class javadoc with all constraints, caller responsibilities, and component implementation requirements.
notes:
## Implementation Plan **Goal**: Add comprehensive Thread-Safety contract section to LifecycleCoordinator class javadoc. **Current State**: Line 30 says "Thread-safe for concurrent registration and lifecycle operations" but doesn't specify constraints. **Solution**: Add detailed Thread-Safety section to class javadoc: ```java /** * Coordinates lifecycle operations across multiple components with dependency ordering. *

* Uses Kahn's topological sort to compute dependency layers: *

    *
  • Startup: Process layers 0→N sequentially, components within layer in parallel
    • *
  • Shutdown: Process layers N→0 sequentially (reverse order)
    • *
  • Circular dependencies: Detected and rejected with LifecycleException
    • *
* *

Thread-Safety Guarantees and Constraints

* *

Coordinator Operations: *

    *
  • All public methods are thread-safe for concurrent access
    • *
  • ConcurrentHashMap provides atomic map operations
    • *
  • Start/stop operations are idempotent via AtomicBoolean guards
    • *
* *

Component Implementation Requirements: *

    *
  • State storage MUST use volatile fields or java.util.concurrent.atomic * classes to ensure cross-thread visibility (see {@link LifecycleComponent})
    • *
  • The {@link LifecycleComponent#getState()} method MUST NOT call back into * the coordinator (deadlock risk - coordinator may hold internal locks)
    • *
  • State transitions in start()/stop() MUST be visible to concurrent getState() calls
    • *
* *

Caller Responsibilities: *

    *
  • Do NOT call unregister() and registerAndStart() concurrently for the same component * (may result in component starting but being removed from tracking)
    • *
  • Do NOT call unregister() while another thread may call start() on the same component * (state-change race - use synchronized external coordination if needed)
    • *
  • Use register() + start() OR registerAndStart(), not both concurrently for same component
    • *
* *

Known Limitations: *

    *
  • State checks in unregister() are not atomic with state transitions - external * synchronization required if unregister can race with start

title: Optimize OptimisticMigratorImpl queue performance
description:
OptimisticMigratorImpl.java:171-187 - synchronizing on CopyOnWriteArrayList defeats its lock-free read optimization.

Problem: CopyOnWriteArrayList designed for many reads/few writes. remove(0) on COWL is O(n) and copies entire array twice. Synchronizing defeats concurrent read benefits. For 100-element queue with high update rate, this becomes a bottleneck.

Fix: Use LinkedBlockingDeque with fixed capacity for O(1) operations and true thread-safety without synchronization.

Impact: Performance bottleneck under high update load.

title: TDD: Memory leak reproduction test + lock cleanup implementation
description:
BUG: CrossProcessMigration.entityMigrationLocks (ConcurrentHashMap<String, ReentrantLock>) grows unbounded. Locks added via computeIfAbsent but never removed. Production memory exhaustion.

FILE: simulation/src/main/java/.../distributed/migration/CrossProcessMigration.java:85

⚠️ CRITICAL: ORIGINAL PLAN HAS RACE CONDITION ⚠️

**deep-analyst identified TOCTOU race in proposed tryLock() cleanup**:
1. Cleanup thread calls tryLock() on lock for entity E1 → succeeds
2. Cleanup marks entry for removal
3. **CONCURRENT**: New migration for E1 calls computeIfAbsent → gets SAME lock object
4. Cleanup removes entry from map
5. Another migration for E1 calls computeIfAbsent → creates NEW lock
6. Two concurrent migrations now hold DIFFERENT locks → **C1 VIOLATED**

**SAFE ALTERNATIVES**:
1. **WeakReference values** (RECOMMENDED): Let GC handle cleanup when no thread holds lock reference
2. **Reference counting**: Track active migrations per entity, remove only when count=0
3. **Accept bounded leak**: Each ReentrantLock ~50 bytes, 1M entities = ~50MB (may be acceptable)
4. **CAS-based cleanup**: Remove only if tryLock() succeeds AND compareAndSet confirms no new migration

**ADDITIONAL RISKS IDENTIFIED**:
- PrimeMover interaction: CrossProcessMigration uses RealTimeController, adding ScheduledExecutorService creates thread outside PrimeMover event loop
- Must analyze interaction between PrimeMover-managed @Entity and cleanup executor

TDD STEPS (REVISED):
1. Write test proving map grows unbounded after N unique entity migrations
2. Write test for C1 preservation: concurrent migrations of same entity still blocked after cleanup
3. Choose safe cleanup strategy (WeakReference recommended)
4. Implement chosen approach
5. Add stress test: 10,000 migrations, verify lock map stabilizes
6. Verify C4 constraint preserved

MUST PRESERVE:
- C1: Per-entity migration locks prevent concurrent migrations (NO RACES)
- C4: testConcurrentMigrationsSameEntity behavior

title: Task 2.2.1: Ghost Epoch/Version Implementation
description:
## Files
- `simulation/src/main/java/.../ghost/GhostBoundarySync.java` (lines 150-151, 253-254)
- `simulation/src/main/java/.../ghost/GhostStateManager.java` (line 403)
- `simulation/src/main/java/.../ghost/DelosSocketTransport.java` (line 338)
- `simulation/src/test/java/.../ghost/GhostBoundarySyncTest.java` (extend)

## Problem
Four locations use placeholder 0L for epoch and version:
1. GhostBoundarySync.java:150-151 (SimulationGhostEntity creation)
2. GhostBoundarySync.java:253-254 (second occurrence)
3. GhostStateManager.java:403
4. DelosSocketTransport.java:338

## Solution
Use bucket-based epoch derivation + atomic version counter.

## Pattern
```java
private static final int EPOCH_SIZE = 100;
private final AtomicLong versionCounter = new AtomicLong(0);

private long deriveEpoch(long bucket) {
    return bucket / EPOCH_SIZE;
}

// Usage:
new SimulationGhostEntity<>(
    e.ghost, e.sourceBubbleId, e.bucket,
    deriveEpoch(e.bucket),           // epoch
    versionCounter.incrementAndGet() // version
)
```

## TDD Requirements
1. Epoch derived correctly from bucket
2. Version increments monotonically
3. Ghost entities have valid epoch/version
4. Backward compatibility

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 4 placeholder locations fixed
- [ ] Epoch derivation consistent
- [ ] Version counter thread-safe
- [ ] Tests verify correct values
- [ ] Existing ghost tests pass

description:
## Files

- `simulation/src/test/java/.../ghost/MigrationLogTest.java` (extend)

## Problem
8 synchronized blocks on `tokens` and `history` objects:
- Line 131: synchronized(tokens) - getOrCreateToken
- Line 146: synchronized(tokens) - update token
- Line 187: synchronized(tokens) - remove token
- Line 206: synchronized(history) - append record
- Line 223: synchronized(history) - query history
- Line 246: synchronized(history) - iterate history
- Line 284: synchronized(history) - filter history
- Line 319: synchronized(history) - clear history

## Solution
Replace with ConcurrentHashMap atomic ops + ConcurrentLinkedDeque.

## Pattern
```java
// tokens already ConcurrentHashMap - use atomic operations:
tokens.computeIfAbsent(entityId, id -> createNewToken(...));
tokens.compute(entityId, (id, existing) -> ...);
tokens.remove(entityId);

// Replace history List with:
private final ConcurrentLinkedDeque<MigrationRecord> history = new ConcurrentLinkedDeque<>();
// Use addLast(), stream(), removeIf()
```

## TDD Requirements
1. Concurrent token creation thread-safe
2. History append thread-safe
3. No lost updates under concurrent access
4. Iteration during modification safe

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 8 synchronized blocks removed
- [ ] ConcurrentHashMap atomic operations
- [ ] ConcurrentLinkedDeque for history
- [ ] Stress tests pass
- [ ] Existing migration tests pass

Medium-High: Core state management, requires comprehensive stress testing

title: H4-GATE: Add pre-commit test gate
description:
## Context
No pre-commit test gate exists. Infrastructure issues reach CI, wasting time.

## Technical Approach
Create git pre-push hook that runs tests before push.

## File to Create
- .git/hooks/pre-push (executable)

## Hook Content
```bash
#!/bin/bash
echo "Running pre-push tests..."
mvn clean test -q
if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "Tests failed. Push aborted."
    exit 1
fi
echo "Tests passed. Proceeding with push."
```

## Documentation
Add to .pm/METHODOLOGY.md:
- How to install hook (make executable)
- How to skip if needed (--no-verify)
- What it catches

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Pre-push hook created
- [ ] Hook is executable
- [ ] Documentation in METHODOLOGY.md
- [ ] Tested with failing test scenario

## Estimated Effort: 30 minutes

On PREPARE_ACK:
  1. sourceBubble.remove(entity)  // REMOVE FIRST
  2. Send COMMIT(token) to dest   // THEN COMMIT

class GhostBoundarySync<ID, Content> {
    void onBucketComplete(long bucket) {
        var nearBoundary = getEntitiesNearBoundary();
        var byNeighbor = groupByNeighborRegion(nearBoundary);
        for (var entry : byNeighbor.entrySet()) {
            sendGhostBatch(entry.getKey(), entry.getValue(), bucket);
        }
        expireStaleGhosts(bucket);  // NEW: Ghost TTL
    }
    
    void onGhostReceived(SimulationGhostEntity ghost) {
        // VON discovery: learn about source bubble
        externalBubbleTracker.onGhostReceived(ghost);
        node.updateGhost(ghost);
    }
}
```

### Boundary Neighbors = Ghost Sources

Ghost layer implements VON's "watchmen" pattern:
- When ghost arrives, you learn about source bubble
- No global bubble registry needed
- Discovery is local and lazy

### Neighbor Consistency (NC) Metric

```java
class GhostLayerHealth {
    float neighborConsistency() {
        // NC = known_neighbors / actual_neighbors (VON metric)
        return knownGhostSources / expectedFirefliesMembers;
    }
    
    int missingExpectedGhosts() {
        return expectedFirefliesMembers - knownGhostSources;
    }
    
    void alertIfDegraded(float threshold) {
        if (neighborConsistency() < threshold) {
            log.warn("Ghost layer degraded: NC={}", neighborConsistency());
            metrics.ghostLayerDegradation().increment();
        }
    }
}
```

**Monitoring**: Alert if NC < 0.9 (missing > 10% of neighbors)

## Dynamics Table

| Event | Trigger | Action |
|-------|---------|--------|
| **Merge** | Drifting entity has high affinity (>0.6) with external bubble | Absorb smaller bubble into larger |
| **Split** | Interaction graph disconnects (union-find) | Create separate bubbles |
| **Reassign** | Entity affinity < 0.5 (drifting) | Transfer to higher-affinity bubble |
| **Migrate** | Bubble load exceeds threshold | Transfer whole bubble to different node |

---

## Implementation

```java
class BubbleDynamicsManager<ID, Content> {
    void processBucketDynamics(long bucket) {
        detectAndProcessMerges(bucket);
        detectAndProcessSplits(bucket);
        reassignDriftingEntities(bucket);
        rebalanceBubbles(bucket);
    }
    
    private void detectAndProcessMerges(long bucket) {
        for (var bubble : node.bubbles.values()) {
            var candidates = externalBubbleTracker.getMergeCandidates(
                bubble.bubbleId, MERGE_THRESHOLD);
            for (var candidate : candidates) {
                if (shouldMerge(bubble, candidate)) {
                    executeMerge(bubble, candidate, bucket);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    private void detectAndProcessSplits(long bucket) {
        for (var bubble : node.bubbles.values()) {
            var components = findDisconnectedComponents(bubble);
            if (components.size() > 1) {
                executeSplit(bubble, components, bucket);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

class MigrationLog<ID> {
    record LogEntry(
        UUID migrationId,      // Idempotency token
        ID entityId,
        UUID sourceBubble,
        UUID targetBubble,
        long bucket,
        long epoch,
        MigrationState state
    )
    
    enum MigrationState { INITIATED, COMPLETED, FAILED }
    
    void append(LogEntry entry);
    List<LogEntry> getInFlightMigrations();
    void markCompleted(UUID migrationId);
}
```

**Key**: Idempotency tokens prevent duplication, epoch prevents stale updates

## Partition Recovery (VON Stock Neighbors)

```java
class StockNeighborList {
    private final List<NodeReference> previouslyKnown = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();
    private final int maxStockSize = 20;  // Bounded memory
    
    void onNeighborLost(NodeReference lost) {
        // Add to stock list for recovery
        if (!previouslyKnown.contains(lost)) {
            previouslyKnown.add(lost);
            if (previouslyKnown.size() > maxStockSize) {
                previouslyKnown.remove(0);  // FIFO eviction
            }
        }
    }
    
    NodeReference getRecoveryContact() {
        // Try stock neighbors when partition detected
        return previouslyKnown.isEmpty() ? null : 
               previouslyKnown.get(random.nextInt(previouslyKnown.size()));
    }
    
    void onNeighborRecovered(NodeReference recovered) {
        previouslyKnown.remove(recovered);  // Back to active
    }
}
```

**Purpose**: VON stock neighbors pattern for partition recovery

public class Bubble<ID extends EntityID, Content> {
    private final UUID bubbleId;
    private final Set<ID> members = ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet();
    private final Map<ID, AffinityTracker> affinities = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final int hostNodeRank;

    // Accessors
    public UUID bubbleId() { return bubbleId; }
    public Set<ID> members() { return Set.copyOf(members); }
    public int size() { return members.size(); }

    // Classification
    public Set<ID> getCoreMembers()     { /* affinity > 0.8 */ }
    public Set<ID> getDriftingMembers() { /* affinity < 0.5 */ }

    // Affinity tracking
    public void recordInteraction(ID entityId, boolean internal);
    public float getAffinity(ID entityId);
}
```

### AffinityTracker.java

```java
public record AffinityTracker(int internal, int external) {
    public float affinity() {
        int total = internal + external;
        return total == 0 ? 0.5f : internal / (float) total;  // 0.5 = uncertain
    }

    public boolean isDrifting()  { return affinity() < 0.5f; }
    public boolean isBoundary()  { return affinity() >= 0.5f && affinity() <= 0.8f; }
    public boolean isCore()      { return affinity() > 0.8f; }

    public AffinityTracker recordInternal() { return new AffinityTracker(internal + 1, external); }
    public AffinityTracker recordExternal() { return new AffinityTracker(internal, external + 1); }
}
```

public class ExternalBubbleTracker {
    private final Map<UUID, ExternalBubbleInfo> knownBubbles = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final Map<BubblePair, AffinityTracker> crossBubbleAffinity = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();

    public record ExternalBubbleInfo(UUID bubbleId, int hostNodeRank, Set<EntityID> ghostedEntities, Instant lastSeen) {}
    public record BubblePair(UUID first, UUID second) {}

    // Called when ghost received - learn about source bubble
    public void onGhostReceived(SimulationGhostEntity<?, ?> ghost);

    // Track cross-bubble affinity for merge detection
    public void recordCrossBubbleInteraction(UUID localBubble, UUID externalBubble);

    // Find merge candidates (high cross-bubble affinity)
    public List<UUID> getMergeCandidates(UUID localBubble, float threshold);

    // Prune stale bubbles
    public void pruneStale(Duration maxAge);
}
```

### SimulationNode.java

```java
public class SimulationNode<ID extends EntityID, Content> {
    private final Forest<TetreeKey<?>, ID, Content> forest;
    private final GhostZoneManager<TetreeKey<?>, ID, Content> ghosts;
    private final DistributedIDGenerator idGenerator;
    private final int nodeRank;

    // Bubble-centric ownership
    private final ConcurrentMap<UUID, Bubble<ID, Content>> bubbles;
    private final ConcurrentMap<ID, UUID> entityToBubble;  // Reverse lookup
    private final ExternalBubbleTracker externalBubbleTracker;

    // Authority is based on bubble membership
    public boolean isAuthoritative(ID entityId) {
        return entityToBubble.containsKey(entityId);
    }

    // Record interaction for affinity tracking
    public void recordInteraction(ID entity1, ID entity2);
}
```

title: Web-based Spatial Inspector: Migrate from JavaFX to Web Browser UI
description:
# Epic: Web-based Spatial Inspector Migration

Migrate spatial visualization from JavaFX to web-based architecture (Javalin + Three.js).
This is a greenfield migration - JavaFX will be completely removed.

## Rationale
- JavaFX apps have launch issues from automated processes
- Web UI enables fully automated testing of backend logic
- Better separation of concerns: backend testable independently
- More portable across platforms
- Modern 3D visualization via Three.js/WebGL

## Architecture
1. **Backend**: Javalin 6.3.0 web server with REST API
2. **Frontend**: Three.js for WebGL 3D visualization
3. **Session Management**: ConcurrentHashMap for multi-user support
4. **GPU Support**: OpenCL rendering exposed via API
5. **Testing**: 100% backend testability without JavaFX

title: Fix ESVT multi-level traversal vertex computation
description: ESVTTraversal.getChildVertices() computes child vertices based on parent TYPE but not actual POSITION. This causes all children of same-type parents at same scale to have identical vertices, breaking multi-level traversal. Fix: Track parent vertices in ESVTStack and compute child vertices relative to actual parent position.
close_reason: Fixed: Added vertex position tracking to ESVTStack and ESVTTraversal. getChildVerticesFromParent() now computes child vertices from actual parent position instead of standard type vertices. Hit rates improved from 2.6% to 61%+ for multi-level trees.

title: Investigate 8-byte vs 12-byte ESVTNodeUnified structure
description: Hypothesis H0: Determine if child types can be derived from TetreeConnectivity.PARENT_TYPE_TO_CHILD_TYPE instead of stored, reducing node from 12 to 8 bytes. Benchmark lookup cost vs storage.
close_reason: H0 VALIDATED: 8-byte nodes confirmed via benchmarks. Table lookup adds only 0.20ns/op (1.04ns vs 0.84ns), negligible 4ns/ray extra. 33% memory savings justifies design. Test file: ESVTNodeStructureBenchmark.java. Decision: ChromaDB decision::esvt::8-byte-node-structure-2025-12

title: FaultTolerantDistributedForest never calls notifyRecoveryComplete -> partition stuck FAILED after successful recovery
description: Discovered while fixing Luciferase-9af5v. FaultTolerantDistributedForest.triggerRecovery (lines 262-269) calls faultHandler.initiateRecovery(id).get() and returns the boolean, but NEVER calls faultHandler.notifyRecoveryComplete(id, success). notifyRecoveryComplete is the only place SimpleFaultHandler/DefaultFaultHandler apply the FAILED->HEALTHY status transition and record recoverySuccess/Failure metrics on PartitionState (SimpleFaultHandler:430, DefaultFaultHandler:496). It is called only in P416PerformanceValidationTest, never in production. Consequence: even after a recovery succeeds, the partition remains marked FAILED and per-partition recovery metrics stay zero. Affects BOTH handlers (the two-phase contract is unwired). FIX: triggerRecovery must call notifyRecoveryComplete(failedPartitionId, success) in the finally/after-get path. Note DefaultFaultHandler ALSO does inline bookkeeping in its initiateRecovery thenApply, so wiring notifyRecoveryComplete there risks double-count -- reconcile one-phase vs two-phase before fixing.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: Fix in PR #281: wire notifyRecoveryComplete + nested-try lock-leak guard + forest-side FAILED->FAILED re-trigger guard (kills an unbounded recovery loop the wiring exposed). Stacked review round-2 clean. Follow-up bead filed for bounded-retry policy (autoRecoveryEnabled/maxRecoveryRetries never consulted).

title: lamportClock dropped cross-process + fed into bucket param (epoch corruption)
description: Two bugs: (a) lamportClock absent from wire schema -- von/Message.java:189 TransportGhost and von/Event.java:165 GhostSync have no lamportClock field; cross-process ghosts lose causal ordering. (b) GhostStateManager.java:270 passes event.lamportClock() into the createGhostEntity 'bucket' parameter -> deriveEpoch(bucket)=bucket/EPOCH_SIZE(100) corrupted for in-process ghosts (P2P path at :493 correctly uses GhostSync.bucket). Stale-detection compares incoherent epochs. NOTE: bead i2y12 referenced for the cross-process half but critic could not locate it -- verify/dedupe. FIX: add lamportClock to TransportGhost+GhostSync and thread through P2PGhostChannel; pass current sim bucket (not lamportClock) at GhostStateManager:270.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: VERDICT: NOT A BUG (epoch half). Traced end-to-end: BubbleGhostCoordinator.java:64 is the ONLY production constructor of EntityUpdateEvent and the ONLY production feed to GhostStateManager.updateGhost; it populates the event's lamportClock FIELD with ghost.bucket() ('Use bucket as lamport clock'). So GhostStateManager.updateGhost:270 passing event.lamportClock() into createGhostEntity's bucket param means deriveEpoch(bucket) receives the REAL bucket -> epoch is CORRECT (createGhostEntity:492-493). The audit/critic claim of 'epoch corruption' read the param names without tracing the caller. The genuine remaining concern -- true lamport-clock causal ordering is NOT propagated for ghosts (the field carries a bucket; cross-process lamportClock is absent from TransportGhost) -- is exactly bead i2y12 (P4), which DEFERS it by design until Phase 7B.3 dead-reckoning needs cross-bubble causality. Closing as not-a-bug; the actionable wire-schema half is tracked by i2y12. Residual: the EntityUpdateEvent.lamportClock field name is a footgun (carries a bucket) -- a rename should ride along with i2y12 when real lamportClock is added.

title: [infra] Real gRPC mTLS handshake unverified repo-wide — Grpc.newServerBuilderForPort + TlsServerCredentials fails over shaded-only netty (UNAVAILABLE)
description: BLOCKER discovered during Luciferase-l9dny. The mTLS credential infra (GrpcCredentialFactory, PeerAuthInterceptor, PeerVerifier, FirefliesPeerVerifier) is wired into GhostCommunicationManager/BalanceCoordinator and compiles, BUT no test anywhere exercises a REAL TLS handshake: CredentialPlumbingTest uses insecureChannel/insecureServer (install-level only), GrpcAuthTest mocks the SSL session (Grpc.TRANSPORT_ATTR_SSL_SESSION). When a real handshake is attempted (l9dny prototype: server via Grpc.newServerBuilderForPort(port, GrpcCredentialFactory.serverAuth(...).credentials()) + client via Grpc.newChannelBuilderForAddress(host,port, mtlsChannel(...))), BOTH the authorized round-trip and a blocking healthCheck fail with Status UNAVAILABLE (handshake never completes) — not the expected delivery / UNAUTHENTICATED. Only grpc-netty-shaded (1.77.0) is on the classpath (simulation AND lucien-distributed); Grpc.newServerBuilderForPort resolves a provider but the non-shaded TlsServerCredentials handshake fails (suspected: shaded-netty TLS/ALPN/SSL-provider gap; needs non-shaded grpc-netty + netty-tcnative-boringssl-static, OR build a shaded GrpcSslContexts SslContext directly instead of the non-shaded credentials API). Root cause buried below grpc layer (UNAVAILABLE has no surfaced cause in logs). IMPACT: l9dny (bubble channel mTLS) AND the existing Ghost/Balance mTLS are all handshake-unproven. Likely warrants an RDR to decide the netty-flavor/TLS-provider strategy repo-wide. Prereq for l9dny.
notes: 2026-06-13 RESOLVED root cause (RDR-023 research-1). Real-handshake diagnostic: cause is client TLS hostname verification — cert CN luciferase-test != dialed authority localhost → CertificateException 'No name matching localhost found' → SSLHandshakeException → UNAVAILABLE. NOT a shaded-netty/provider/ALPN issue (native OpenSslEngine/tcnative handshakes fine; same non-shaded Grpc.* path works WITH overrideAuthority; shaded GrpcSslContexts also works). ACCEPT_ANY_CERT (plain X509TrustManager) bypasses chain validation but NOT hostname verification. FIX = Strategy C: make ACCEPT_ANY_CERT an X509ExtendedTrustManager with no-op endpoint-identification overloads (correct for RDR-005 model — identity via PeerVerifier, not cert CN; no dep change). Implementation + real-handshake test pending via RDR-023 (gate then implement). See docs/rdr/RDR-023.
close_reason: RDR-023 Strategy C implemented + merged (PR #263): GrpcCredentialFactory.ACCEPT_ANY_CERT → X509ExtendedTrustManager with no-op endpoint-id overloads, disabling client TLS hostname verification (root cause: cert CN ≠ dialed authority). Real-handshake test proves the mTLS transport works (authorized OK + PeerVerifier-rejected→UNAUTHENTICATED) — first proven gRPC mTLS handshake in the repo. Bytecode-verified server-side client-cert handling unchanged. No dep change. Unblocks l9dny; hardens Ghost/Balance.

title: [simulation] 2PC timeout/rollback-failure paths write no ABORT tombstone — recovery cannot distinguish timed-out-mid-rollback from clean-rollback-then-crash
description: Raised by both reviewers (code-review-expert + substantive-critic) during Luciferase-f5nj7. CrossProcessMigration's PREPARE_TIMEOUT (:768-773), ABORT_TIMEOUT (:885-895), and ROLLBACK_FAILED (:940-943) paths complete the migration future WITHOUT writing any WAL resolution record (walRecordAbort is only reached on the clean rollback path at :928). So loadIncomplete() returns the dangling PREPARE for: (a) clean rollback that crashed before WAL flush, (b) timed-out abort, (c) failed rollback (orphaned entity). Recovery re-attempts rollback in ALL cases — idempotent only if source.addEntity is idempotent (UNVERIFIED). Gaps: recovery cannot route timed-out/orphaned txns differently from clean rollbacks; operators cannot count timed-out aborts separately from completed aborts in the WAL audit trail. Pinned-as-intended for now by CrossProcessMigration2PCInstrumentationTest.timedOutMigrationLeavesPrepareIncompleteForRecovery (f5nj7). Consider: write a distinct TIMEOUT/ORPHANED resolution record on timeout/rollback-failure so recovery + audit can distinguish, and verify source re-add idempotency. Relates to RDR-004/RDR-019 durability lineage.
close_reason: Decided A (defer+document): 2PC+WAL is scaffold — loadIncomplete has no production consumer, cross-process add stubbed, so a tombstone is speculative infra. Shipped breadcrumbs documenting the deliberate deferral (PR #252). Round-2 clean review. Tombstone build deferred to productionization → successor Luciferase-jv5rh (blocked on ut59r).

title: Phase 1: Clock injection into LifecycleCoordinator — ctor param + delegate chain
description:
## Context

Production file: simulation/src/main/java/com/hellblazer/luciferase/simulation/lifecycle/LifecycleCoordinator.java
Test file: simulation/src/test/java/com/hellblazer/luciferase/simulation/lifecycle/LifecycleCoordinatorTest.java
Clock interface: com.hellblazer.luciferase.common.time.Clock (common module, has currentTimeMillis() + nanoTime(); Clock.system() factory)
TestClock: simulation/src/test/java/com/hellblazer/luciferase/simulation/distributed/integration/TestClock.java (has advance(deltaMs), setTime(ms), nanoTime() returning nanos consistently)

## What changes

Add `Clock clock` as a new field and new constructor parameter to LifecycleCoordinator.

Current master constructor (line 168):
  public LifecycleCoordinator(long componentTimeoutMs, ViewStabilityGate viewStabilityGate)

New master constructor:
  public LifecycleCoordinator(long componentTimeoutMs, ViewStabilityGate viewStabilityGate, Clock clock)
  → this.clock = Objects.requireNonNullElseGet(clock, Clock::system);

All existing ctors delegate to the new master with Clock.system() as the third arg:
  public LifecycleCoordinator() → this(DEFAULT_COMPONENT_TIMEOUT_MS, null, Clock.system())
  public LifecycleCoordinator(long componentTimeoutMs) → this(componentTimeoutMs, null, Clock.system())
  public LifecycleCoordinator(ViewStabilityGate gate) → this(DEFAULT_COMPONENT_TIMEOUT_MS, gate, Clock.system())
  public LifecycleCoordinator(long componentTimeoutMs, ViewStabilityGate gate) → this(componentTimeoutMs, gate, Clock.system())

No behavioral change in stop() yet — that is Phase 2.

Add import: import com.hellblazer.luciferase.common.time.Clock;

The common module is already a dependency of simulation (verify: grep 'common' simulation/pom.xml).

## TDD approach (write the test FIRST, watch it compile but not test any new behavior yet)

Write a new test method in LifecycleCoordinatorTest.java:

  clockInjectionExposedViaNewCtor()

Test body:
  var testClock = new TestClock(1_000_000L);  // arbitrary start nanos-friendly value
  var coordinator = new LifecycleCoordinator(5000L, null, testClock);
  // Phase 1 just validates that the coordinator accepts the clock without error.
  // The clock field is not yet observable from outside; this test just asserts
  // the coordinator can be constructed and used normally.
  coordinator.register(new MockComponent("A", List.of(), startOrder, stopOrder));
  coordinator.start();
  coordinator.stop(5000);
  assertEquals(1, stopOrder.size());  // normal operation unaffected

This test MUST compile before making the impl change. Once the ctor exists it will pass.
Import TestClock from com.hellblazer.luciferase.simulation.distributed.integration.TestClock
(already on the test classpath in the simulation module).

## Test command

  mvn test -pl simulation -Dtest=LifecycleCoordinatorTest#clockInjectionExposedViaNewCtor -Dsurefire.rerunFailingTestsCount=0

## Design test scenarios covered by this phase

None of (a-e) are fully validated here — Phase 1 is pure plumbing. Scenarios (a-e) land in Phases 2-3.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] LifecycleCoordinator has a new public 3-arg ctor (componentTimeoutMs, ViewStabilityGate, Clock)
- [ ] All 4 existing ctors delegate to the new master passing Clock.system() — no behavioral change
- [ ] `private final Clock clock` field present, initialized from the parameter
- [ ] clockInjectionExposedViaNewCtor test green
- [ ] Full simulation test suite still green: mvn test -pl simulation

## Dependencies

Blocked by: Luciferase-43bat (parent)
Blocks: Luciferase-q7g4z (Phase 2)

title: [sim] ViewCommitteeConsensus: inFlightByEntity written before pendingProposals — onViewChange race can permanently block an entity
description: RDR-020 holistic phase-boundary review finding (code-review-expert, 2026-06-09). PRE-EXISTING (not introduced by RDR-020; the per-entity in-flight mutex is Luciferase-0frcy.94). In ViewCommitteeConsensus.requestConsensus, inFlightByEntity.putIfAbsent(entityId, proposalId) commits the entity slot BEFORE pendingProposals.put(proposalId, tracking). If onViewChange fires in the window between: (1) it iterates pendingProposals — proposal not there yet; (2) skips inFlightByEntity.remove for this entity; (3) entity permanently stuck in inFlightByEntity with no surviving future to release it. No path scans inFlightByEntity for orphans. Nanosecond window (Fireflies virtual synchrony) but logically broken under any concurrency. Fix: write pendingProposals.put BEFORE inFlightByEntity.putIfAbsent (onViewChange iterates pendingProposals first), or wrap both in one lock scope. Verify line numbers (~206/214) and that RDR-020 did not touch this ordering.
close_reason: Fixed: ViewCommitteeConsensus.requestConsensus writes pendingProposals before inFlightByEntity (with undo on duplicate-in-flight) + post-write view re-check releasing both on view change. Commit 486e49ca. Race genuinely closed per stacked-review (all 4 interleavings sound). Test: testViewChangeReleasesInFlightEntitySlot. 180 committee tests green.

title: [sim] ViewCommitteeSelector.selectCommittee/bftSubset draws committee from full ring — offline member can still vote (active-only composition gap)
description: RDR-020 S6 review finding (substantive-critic, 2026-06-09). S6 tightened ViewCommitteeSelector.isNodeInView to context.active() so a proposal naming an evicted node as source/target is rejected. But committee COMPOSITION is still active-unfiltered: selectCommittee -> context.bftSubset(viewDiadem) -> Ring.succ() iterates the full ring NavigableMap with an always-true predicate; DynamicContextImpl.offline() flips Tracked.active=false but does NOT remove the member from the ring. So an evicted-but-not-GC'd member can still appear in the committee, receive a forwarded vote, and contribute to quorum as a VOTER (distinct from the node being migrated, which S6 now gates). Fix options: (a) pass context::isActive as the bftSubset filter predicate in selectCommittee() — one-line, cleanest seam; or (b) verify voting member is active at vote-receipt before recording. Needs its own gate-then-accept (verify the Delos bftSubset predicate overload exists/semantics). Out of RDR-020 S6 scope (S6 bead i4prr was narrowly isNodeInView). Evidence: DynamicContextImpl.offline():808-813, uniqueSuccessors():732-739, Context.bftSubset():111-124.
close_reason: Fixed via option (b): CommitteeVotingProtocol.recordVote drops votes from inactive committee members (context.isActive gate). Commit 486e49ca. Safety-correct, fails closed; more conservative than option (a) per stacked-review (option a could shrink committee toward committeeQuorum(2)==1). Liveness tradeoff documented; committee-resizing-under-churn tracked by Luciferase-0frcy.134. Test: testInactiveCommitteeMemberVoteDroppedFromQuorum. 180 committee tests green.

title: RDR-019 gate-S1 follow-up: source-side ghost re-derivation after compaction prunes a departed entity (null->GHOST forward path)
description:
ACCEPTED GAP from RDR-019 P2.1 (Luciferase-ybipo, decision B). After Phase 2 WAL compaction prunes a committed DEPARTURE+COMMIT pair, the source node's FSM has getState(id)==null on restart, so the live DEPARTED->GHOST forward path is not reconstructible via the FSM (transition() returns notFound for untracked entities by the single-owner invariant; there is deliberately no null->GHOST transition).

WHY ACCEPTED (not fixed now): entity is owned at the TARGET (no ownership-invariant violation); only source-side ghost adjacency tracking is lost; ghost adjacency is re-derivable by the neighbor layer and is not load-bearing on FSM DEPARTED bookkeeping. Normally DEPARTED->GHOST is a live near-immediate follow-on to commit, occurring BEFORE compaction's watermark would prune the pair.

CONSTRAINT enforced in P2.3 compaction (0ejd2): the prune watermark must be conservative enough that recently-departed, still-adjacent entities are not pruned (watermark > ghost-adjacency lifetime, or only prune pairs whose entities are confirmed non-adjacent).

WHEN TO DO: if a workload surfaces lost source-side ghosts after compaction+restart, add a neighbor-layer ghost re-derivation step on recovery (NOT a null->GHOST FSM transition). Sites: EntityMigrationStateMachine.isValidTransition DEPARTED case (comment); GhostStateListener.reconcileGhostState; the neighbor/adjacency reconstruction path.

Refs: docs/rdr/RDR-019 §Critical Assumptions (a) / §Revision History S1.
close_reason: Approach B (harden+pin) shipped: WalCompactionSourceGhostGapTest characterizes the accepted gap + benignity; reconcileGhostState breadcrumb marks the future re-derivation hook. No production re-derivation built (deferred, no surfacing workload). Merged PR #247.

title: RDR-017: lifecycle-integrate BubbleMigrator (BubbleMigratorAdapter) — stop migrator before WAL on shutdown
description: P2 stacked-review Sig-2: NodeBootstrap.assemble(4-arg) wires bubbleMigrator.setPersistenceManager(pm) but does NOT register the migrator as a lifecycle component. On Manager.close() the coordinator stops the PM adapter (closes WAL) with no knowledge of the migrator; an in-flight migration can then call logMigrationCommit() after the WAL is closed → commit fails → ENTITY_DEPARTURE-without-COMMIT split-brain precondition (the RDR-016 R2 hazard). Today latent: NodeBootstrap.main() throws, so no in-flight migration exists at shutdown. Before main() is wired live, make BubbleMigrator a LifecycleComponent (BubbleMigratorAdapter) at a layer ABOVE PersistenceManager so the coordinator stops/drains it first (reverse-order shutdown), OR have the node shutdown path call migrator.shutdown() before Manager.close(). title: BubbleSplitter: snapshot/partition taken pre-lock (TOCTOU) + no concurrency test for the n7io1 split lock
description:
Round-2 stacked review of Luciferase-n7io1 surfaced two residual gaps in BubbleSplitter.execute (both reviewers, non-blocking):

I-1 (Significant): the entity snapshot (getAllEntityRecords), split-plane calc (strategy.calculate), partition (partitionEntities), centroid/key allocation, and new-bubble creation all happen BEFORE MutationLocks.lock(sourceBubble, newBubble) is acquired (BubbleSplitter.java:167 vs :276). A concurrent migration/merge can move entities out of sourceBubble in that window. This is rollback-protected (accountant.moveBetweenBubbles returns false -> abort+rollback, no data loss) but causes spurious split aborts under contention and is inconsistent with the re-validate-under-lock discipline established by the S-2 fix in MultiDirectionalMigration.commitMigration. A proper fix needs restructuring: the new bubble does not exist to lock until after the snapshot-derived plane/key are computed. Options: (a) acquire the source lock early for a stable snapshot, recompute plane/key under it; (b) re-validate entity presence inside the move loop while preserving the snapshot-based conservation arithmetic.

I-2: the rewritten BubbleMutationLockConcurrencyTest covers BubbleLifecycle.transferEntities + an inline manual locker, but NOT BubbleSplitter.execute — the C1 fix (the actual lock added in dac9fb73) has no direct concurrency test. Add an integration-level test exercising concurrent split + migration on the same source bubble (needs a real EntityAccountant + TetreeBubbleGrid).

Source: n7io1 stacked-review round 2, commits e3d6417a/dac9fb73.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: Fixed (option b): re-validate each entity's source membership under MutationLocks.lock(source,new) and SKIP entities that escaped during the snapshot->lock window, instead of aborting+rolling back the whole split. This is the multi-entity analogue of the single-entity stale-intent guard in MultiDirectionalMigration.commitMigration (n7io1 S-2). Option (a) (lock-before-snapshot, like BubbleMerger) is not available: the new bubble doesn't exist until the snapshot-derived plane/centroid/key are computed, and locking source alone early would break n7io1's ascending-UUID global ordering (deadlock). I-2 closed by new BubbleSplitConcurrencyTest (deterministic skip-path via SplitPlaneStrategy injection seam + concurrent split-vs-migration stress). Full simulation suite 3090/0/0. KNOWN RESIDUAL (deferred, demand-driven): the new bubble's SFC key/centroid is still derived from the pre-lock snapshot, so escaped entities skew it slightly — spatial-locality quality gap only, not a safety/conservation issue (documented in BubbleSplitter.java at the centroid computation).

title: Migration escape test uses RDG-AABB approximation, not exact tetrahedral containment
description: RDR-015 P3 substantive-critic finding #3. TetrahedralContainmentChecker.checkMigrations tests entity escape via BubbleBounds.fromTetreeKey(cellKey).contains(pos), which applies toRDG (a basis ROTATION) then an AABB test — an OUTER approximation of the tetrahedron. Consequences: (1) coordinate-space mixing — the partition is tiled in RAW Cartesian coords but escape is tested in RDG-rotated AABB space; (2) false negatives — an entity geometrically in a face-neighbor still lies inside S's RDG-AABB, so it does not register as escaped until ~1.5 cell-edges out (this is why DirectedMigrationRegressionTest cannot assert strict face-adjacency); (3) asymmetric escape timing across reflected directions; (4) bounded ping-pong (COOLDOWN_TICKS=30 caps it). Fix: switch escape to EXACT tet containment — escaped iff tetree.locateTetrahedron(pos, partitionLevel).tmIndex() != bubble.spatialKey(). This is consistent with the router (already queries locateTetrahedron at L) and enables a strictly face-adjacent AC5 directed test. CAVEAT: must also rework the spatial-hysteresis gate in TetrahedralMigration.migrationCandidate (HYSTERESIS_DIST overshoot vs the fixed-cell AABB) — exact containment makes AABB-overshoot=0 for an entity just over a face, so it would re-suppress; the 7wzml.185 hysteresis test suite (TetrahedralMigrationTest) pins current semantics and must be updated in lock-step. Refs: TetrahedralContainmentChecker.java checkMigrations; TetrahedralMigration.java migrationCandidate; BubbleBounds.contains/fromTetreeKey; RDGCoordinates.toRDG. RDR: RDR-015 (no F-number; review finding).
notes: BLOCKED-BY-DEPENDENCY (2026-06-06): this RDR-015 followup modifies the fixed-cell escape path (TetrahedralContainmentChecker.checkMigrations testing BubbleBounds.fromTetreeKey(spatialKey), TetrahedralMigration.migrationCandidate hysteresis) introduced by the RDR-015 IMPLEMENTATION, which is unmerged (PR #202, branch feature/j8p8n-rdr-015-coordinate-space). main still has the OLD adaptive-bounds checkMigrations(bounds.contains(position)). Do 6kod9 stacked on #202 AFTER it merges, or rebase once merged — not off main.

title: Dynamic topology (split/merge) re-breaks the RDR-015 same-level migration partition
description: RDR-015 made the bubble grid a single-level spatial partition (Option B) so face-crossing entities migrate to a real neighbor. That invariant is an INIT-and-migration guarantee for a NON-splitting grid (RDR-015 ## Scope decision). BubbleSplitter.splitBubble inserts split children at startLevel = parentLevel+1 (BubbleSplitter.java:219), i.e. a FINER level — the moment TopologyExecutor (simulation/src/main/java/com/hellblazer/luciferase/simulation/topology/TopologyExecutor.java) fires a split during a run, the partition becomes mixed-level again and migration routing (which queries at the single partitionLevel L via TetreeBubbleGrid.getPartitionLevel) silently mis-routes / drops the finer cell. Open design question (defer to a follow-up RDR): redefine split as same-level SIBLING replacement (replace one level-L bubble with its level-L neighbors) vs make the router handle a post-split mixed-level grid. Until resolved, a steady-state simulation that runs splits must NOT be assumed to migrate correctly. Refs: BubbleSplitter.java:219, TopologyExecutor; TetreeBubbleGrid.getPartitionLevel()/createBubbles(WorldBounds). Driving bead: Luciferase-0frcy.131. RDR: docs/rdr/RDR-015-simulation-bubble-grid-coordinate-space.md ## Scope decision.
notes: Two reasons not ready off main (2026-06-06): (1) RDR-015 implementation (PR #202) unmerged — this followup assumes the single-level partition + getPartitionLevel router; (2) the bead itself states the resolution is an OPEN DESIGN QUESTION to defer to a follow-up RDR (same-level sibling replacement vs router handling mixed-level grid). Needs an RDR-create, not blind implementation.

title: [bug] [simulation] MultiBubbleSimulation commits ZERO successful migrations via tick() — migration-commit path appears dead

This makes getTotalMigrations() effectively always 0 in production tick loops — the migration subsystem may be dead on the live path. comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE (investigated 2026-06-06): coordinate-space mismatch — the migration path is dead-on-arrival for any WorldBounds smaller than the tetree cell scale.

EVIDENCE (diagnostic over 2000 ticks, 8 bubbles, 200 entities, WorldBounds 0-30): total=200, escapedBounds=0, migrations=0. ZERO entities ever leave their bubble bounds.

CHAIN:
1. EntityPopulationManager.populateEntities (EntityPopulationManager.java:105-110) generates positions uniformly in WorldBounds: x = min + rand*size, with WorldBounds(0,100)/(0,30).
2. EntityDistribution.EntitySpec (EntityDistribution.java:67) documents position as "in RDGCS coordinates" (tetree scale); entities are assigned to bubbles via Tetree.locateTetrahedron.
3. Bubble bounds are the tet region at tetree SFC scale. Observed: L1 [(-741455,0,0),(741455,1482910,741455)], L2 [(-370728,..)], L0 [(-1482910,..),(2965821,..)] — tens of thousands to ~3,000,000 units wide.
4. TetrahedralContainmentChecker.checkMigrations (line 110) emits a MigrationRecord only when !bounds.contains(position). Entities confined to [0,100]^3 sit in a microscopic corner of every bubble's million-unit bounds and never satisfy this -> no candidates -> getTotalMigrations stays 0.

WorldBounds (entity coordinate space) is fully decoupled from the bubble grid's spatial domain (RDGCS/tetree). No transform maps world<->RDGCS.

SECONDARY BUG: TetreeBubbleGrid.createBubbles distributes bubbles across MIXED levels (createTetAtLevel(level, idx)); the L0 root spatially contains everything and L1/L2 nest/overlap; duplicate keys observed (two bubbles each at CompactTetreeKey[L1,tm:A] and [L2,tm:A]). The grid is not a same-level spatial partition -> containment is ambiguous even if an entity escaped.

RECOMMENDED FIX (architectural — warrants an RDR/design decision, not a patch):
- Option B (preferred): build the bubble grid as a same-level spatial PARTITION over the world domain (adjacent same-level tets tiling WorldBounds) so boundary crossings route to a real neighbor; OR
- Option C: introduce an explicit, consistently-applied world<->RDGCS transform across population, physics (RandomWalk clamps to WorldBounds), bubble bounds, and containment.

title: [render] GPU esvo_ray_traversal.cl NEAR-pointer child resolution omits current.nodeIdx — wrong child for non-root interior nodes (+ GPU far-pointer N>0 parity needs hardware verification)

title: [lucien] HierarchicalZBuffer.renderOccluder silently no-ops for standard camera matrices (z-sign) — DSOC occlusion culling dead when enabled
description: Substantive-critic discovery during Wave-17 .148. HierarchicalZBuffer.projectBounds (~:286-296) admits only corners where projected[2]>0, and projectPoint (~:335) stores raw post-divide NDC z. Under a standard right-handed orthographic/perspective projection, world-positive z maps to NEGATIVE NDC z, so every corner fails the >0 guard, projectBounds returns null, renderOccluder returns early (~:177-179), the Z-buffer is never written, updateHierarchy propagates all-zero, and isOccluded always returns false. Net: DSOC occlusion culling is a NO-OP for any scene using a standard camera matrix. DSOC is disabled-by-default so impact is opt-in, but when enabled it silently does nothing (looks-works-does-nothing class). This is OUT OF SCOPE for .148 (which correctly fixes the per-level index mapping and is now non-vacuously tested). Fix: correct the projectBounds z-sign guard to the actual projection convention (negate to <0 for right-handed, or store depth as 1-NDC_z so in-frustum geometry is positive); add an integration test asserting renderOccluder writes non-zero depth for a known in-frustum occluder AND that a behind-object is reported occluded. RISK: occlusion tests currently passing because occlusion is a no-op may need updating. Evidence: HierarchicalZBuffer.java:286-296,335; critic T2 wave17-p2-correctness-substantive-critique-2026-06-04.md.

title: [portal] buildFromVoxels returns a non-null BuildResult wrapping a null structure on failure — looks successful to unchecked callers
description:
portal/src/main/java/com/hellblazer/luciferase/portal/esvo/bridge/ESVOBridge.java:227-231
Severity: Medium | Category: serialization

The failure is encoded only in a free-text message string, not a typed success flag. This is the silent-failure/placeholder anti-pattern.

Fix: Add an explicit success/ok boolean (or Optional payload) to BuildResult and have callers gate on it; do not return a null payload behind an otherwise-success-shaped result.

title: [portal] planarize(int) computes maxChange from diff(newPos,newPos) — always 0, divergence guard dead
description:
portal/src/main/java/com/hellblazer/luciferase/portal/mesh/util/Canonicalize.java:116-128
Severity: Medium | Category: correctness / dead safety guard

In planarize(Polyhedron, int numIterations) the per-iteration maxChange loop does VectorMath.diff(newPos, newPos) (line 118) which is identically the zero vector, so maxChange is always 0.0. The subsequent guard (line 126) '(maxChange > MAX_VERTEX_CHANGE)' can therefore NEVER trigger, defeating the documented early-termination on erroneous large vertex movement (the NaN check still works). The threshold-based canonicalize() path (lines 72-77) computes maxChange correctly against currentPositions, confirming the int-iteration variant is the broken one. The algorithm still applies setVertexPositions(newPositions), so geometry updates; only the runaway-divergence safety net is inert.

Fix: Capture pre-iteration positions and compare: diff(newPos, oldPositions.get(i)). Mirror the pattern in canonicalize() (snapshot currentPositions before setVertexPositions). Then the MAX_VERTEX_CHANGE guard becomes meaningful.
