title: [lucien] TOCTOU race in fault status escalation (report* methods)
description:
lucien/src/main/java/com/hellblazer/luciferase/lucien/balancing/fault/SimpleFaultHandler.java:264-302
Severity: Medium | Category: concurrency

reportBarrierTimeout/reportSyncFailure/reportHeartbeatFailure do computeIfAbsent(state) then read state.status (volatile) WITHOUT holding the PartitionState lock, branch on HEALTHY vs SUSPECTED, then call transitionToSuspected/transitionToFailed. PartitionState.updateStatus is synchronized but the read-decide-act sequence is not atomic. Two concurrent reports both observing HEALTHY both transition to SUSPECTED and both call recordFailure() (double-counting metrics). A HEALTHY+SUSPECTED interleaving can lose the escalation to FAILED. The state machine guarantee (HEALTHY->SUSPECTED->FAILED, single failure increment per report) is not honored under concurrency despite the class advertising 'thread-safe concurrent access'.

Fix: Move the read-old-status / decide / transition into a synchronized block on the PartitionState instance (e.g. a synchronized escalate(reason) method on PartitionState that reads its own status and applies the next transition), so the CAS-style escalation is atomic per partition.

Verify evidence: Confirmed by reading SimpleFaultHandler.java. The three report* methods perform a non-atomic read-decide-act. reportBarrierTimeout (264-272): `var state = partitions.computeIfAbsent(partitionId, PartitionState::new); var oldStatus = state.status; if (oldStatus == PartitionStatus.HEALTHY) { transitionToSuspected(...) } else if (oldStatus == PartitionStatus.SUSPECTED) { transitionToFailed(...) }`. Identical shape in reportSyncFailure (278-286) and reportHeartbeatFailure (293-302). `status` is `volatile PartitionStatus status` (line 53). The mutators are individually synchronized — `synchronized void updateStatus` (70), `synchronized void recordFailure` (75) — but NO lock spans the read of state.status through the transition call, so the compound check-then-act is not atomic. transitionToSuspected (424-427) calls updateStatus(SUSPECTED) then recordFailure(); transitionToFailed (441-444) likewise. Two concurrent reports both observing HEALTHY both invoke transitionToSuspected -> recordFailure() runs twice (metric double-count); a HEALTHY+SUSPECTED interleaving can lose the escalation to FAILED. The class explicitly advertises 'Provides thread-safe concurrent access' (line 20), which th

design:
### SpatialTumbler Region ID Collision for Negative Coordinates
- Location (verifier-confirmed): **sim:tumbler/SpatialTumbler.java:136-141**
- Category: correctness · unit=persistence-misc
- Root cause: computeRegionId casts int grid coordinates to long then masks with 0xFFFFF (20 bits). A negative grid coordinate gx=-1 (from a position just below the world origin) masks to 0xFFFFF (1048575), which is identical to gx=1048575 (a very large positive coordinate). Worlds that include any negative coordinates (e.g. centered at origin) will experience pervasive region ID collisions.
- Fix: Use a hash function that handles signed integers without truncation, e.g. Morton3D on (gx+offset, gy+offset, gz+offset) with a bias that shifts the grid to non-negative space, or use Long.hashCode on a sign-extending long value.

This produces hash collisions for any world that includes coordinates below the origin (e.g., a world centered at origin, which is the common case). Lines 137-139 show gx/gy/gz are computed via `Math.floor(position.x / regionGridS

**Build/verify**: `mvn test -pl simulation -Dtest=<NewTest> -Dsurefire.rerunFailingTestsCount=0`.
acceptance_criteria: Use a hash function that handles signed integers without truncation, e.g. Morton3D on (gx+offset, gy+offset, gz+offset) with a bias that shifts the grid to non-negative space, or use Long.hashCode on a sign-extending lon Covered by a regression test (fails pre-fix, passes post-fix).
close_reason: computeRegionId biases each signed grid coord by 2^19 into non-negative 20-bit window before masking (canonical Morton-bias fix per acceptance); removes sign-extension aliasing of negatives within window. Test: SpatialTumblerRegionIdTest. Residual: 20-bit packing has inherent 2^20 period; coords >2^19 apart still alias (unfixable in bit budget).

### BucketSynchronizedController: TOCTOU race in bucket detection + overrun clock drift
- Location (verifier-confirmed): **sim:bubble/BucketSynchronizedController.java:77-86**
- Category: concurrency · unit=bubble-core · flagged by critic
- Root cause: Two separate reads of currentBucket (line 77) and computation of currentBucketNum (line 76) happen between two unsynchronized memory reads. advanceBucket(long) (line 121) allows external callers to advance currentBucket between the two reads. If advanceBucket fires between the reads, synchronizeAtBucket is called with a stale bucket number and the simulation time is aligned to the wrong bucket. Additionally, tickLoop() always sleeps the full tickPeriodNs (line 86) regardless of how long tick work took, while the parent RealTimeController uses deadline-based scheduling (nextDeadline -= sleepNs) to subtract work time from the next sleep. BucketSynchronizedController regresses to fixed-period sleeping, causing monotonic drift proportional to load. There are zero tests for this class.
- Fix: Replace the two-read pattern with a single CAS: read currentBucket, compute expected new bucket, and CAS-update in one step so only one thread applies a given bucket transition. Restore deadline-based scheduling from the parent: record startNs before tick work, compute sleepNs = tickPeriodNs - elapsed, sleep only the remainder. Add comprehensive tests for bucket synchronization including advanceBucket() racing.
- Verifier evidence: Inspected /Users/hal.hildebrand/git/Luciferase/simulation/src/main/java/com/hellblazer/luciferase/simulation/bubble/BucketSynchronizedController.java lines 74-91.

design:
### RealTimeController: non-daemon thread with self-deadlock potential in stop()
- Location (verifier-confirmed): **sim:bubble/RealTimeController.java:192, 201-212**
- Category: concurrency · unit=bubble-core · flagged by critic
- Root cause: tickThread.setDaemon(false) (line 192) means the JVM cannot exit while the controller is running. stop() calls tickThread.join(1000) (line 205) without first interrupting the thread. If a TickListener calls stop() from within the tick callback (a realistic scenario for ghost coordinators, frame monitors, or split triggers), tickThread.join(1000) will deadlock because the calling thread IS the tick thread — it waits for itself to finish. After 1000ms the InterruptedException catch silently swallows the interrupt and the method returns, but the tick thread continues running.
- Fix: Before join(), call tickThread.interrupt(). In tickLoop(), the InterruptedException catch already breaks the loop correctly (line 248). Change thread to daemon (setDaemon(true)) unless intentional JVM-pinning is needed. Guard against self-join: if (Thread.currentThread() == tickThread) { running.set(false); return; }
- Verifier evidence: Inspected /Users/hal.hildebrand/git/Luciferase/simulation/src/main/java/com/hellblazer/luciferase/simulation/bubble/RealTimeController.java lines 191-213 and 225-253.

design:
### Unsynchronized long counters in EnhancedBubbleMigrationIntegration mutated from multiple threads
- Location (verifier-confirmed): **sim:bubble/EnhancedBubbleMigrationIntegration.java:103-106**
- Category: concurrency · unit=bubble-migration · flagged by expert
- Root cause: totalMigrationsInitiated, totalMigrationsCompleted, totalMigrationsRolledBack, and totalTimeoutsProcessed are plain long fields. They are mutated from processMigrations() (called from the tick thread) and from onEntityStateTransition() and onViewChangeRollback() (FSM listener callbacks, potentially called from a different thread). Under the JMM, non-volatile long writes/reads are not guaranteed atomic on 64-bit JVMs without synchronization. The getMetrics() output may read torn values.
- Fix: Replace the four plain longs with AtomicLong and use incrementAndGet()/addAndGet(). Alternatively, annotate the class as requiring single-threaded access and document the guarantee, but that is inconsistent with the ConcurrentHashMap usage elsewhere.
- Verifier evidence: The four plain long fields at lines 103-106 are confirmed unsynchronized. The cross-thread write path is real but currently latent: `onViewChangeRollback` (line 352: `totalMigrationsRolledBack += rolledBackCount`) is a `MigrationStateListener` callback intended to fire on Fireflies view-change events from a membership thread. While no production caller yet wires `migrationFsm.onViewChange()` to a view-change event (grep finds it only in comments)

### cleanupRemovedEntities() mutates map while computeVelocity() iterates it
- Location (verifier-confirmed): **sim:behavior/FlockingBehavior.java:170-172**
- Category: concurrency · unit=behavior-spatial · flagged by expert
- Root cause: `cleanupRemovedEntities()` calls `previousVelocities.keySet().retainAll(activeEntityIds)` and `currentVelocities.keySet().retainAll(activeEntityIds)` without coordination with concurrently-running `computeVelocity()` threads that are iterating `previousVelocities` (via `get`) and writing `currentVelocities` (via `put`). While ConcurrentHashMap is individually thread-safe, `retainAll` on its key-set performs a multi-step iteration-plus-removal that will race with ongoing puts, potentially removing an entry that was just inserted for the current tick.

Line 179: `computeVelocity` writes `currentVelocities.put(entityId, new Vector3f(velocity))` concurrently. Line 287: `computeAlignment` reads `previousVelocities.get(neighbor.id())`.

The race is genuine. `ConcurrentHashMap.keySet().retainAll()` performs a multi-step iterate-and-remove

**Build/verify**: `mvn test -pl simulation -Dtest=<NewTest> -Dsurefire.rerunFailingTestsCount=0` (assertions ON).
acceptance_criteria: Only clean up at tick boundaries (after swapVelocityBuffers, before any computeVelocity calls), and hold the same lock used to guard the swap. - Location (verifier-confirmed): **sim:spatial/DeadReckoningEstimator.java:129-160**
- Category: concurrency · unit=behavior-spatial · flagged by expert
- Root cause: predict() reads the current CorrectionState for a ghost entity, computes a partial correction, then puts an updated CorrectionState (or removes it). This is a three-step read-modify-write on a ConcurrentHashMap. title: 2:1 balance can't resolve a coarse cell whose subdivide is refused (all entities in one child octant) — burns maxRounds
description: Surfaced by the bunny 2:1 demo (BunnyTwoOneBalanceDemoTest: 15 violations -> 4 residual) and confirmed by reviewers. Octree.handleNodeSubdivision (and Tetree's) REFUSE to subdivide when all of a node's entities map to a single child octant (childEntityMap.size()==1) or coincide at child granularity — it returns early, creates no children, leaves hasChildren=false. If such a coarse cell has a fine (level-diff>1) neighbor, the 2:1 violation is GENUINE but the balance loop can never resolve it: subdivide is a no-op, hasChildren stays false (correctly not a hthxs false-positive — it really is an unrefined leaf), so the violation re-reports every round and CrossPartitionBalancePhase burns all maxRounds without converging. Root issue: 2:1 refinement here is entity-redistribution-gated, but the 2:1 constraint is GEOMETRIC — to satisfy it you must be able to create finer (possibly empty) child cells regardless of entity distribution. WHAT: either (a) give the balance path a geometric 'refine one level' that creates the child cell covering the boundary even when entity redistribution is a no-op, or (b) detect unresolvable cells and stop re-queuing them (mark resolved-as-possible) so the loop converges instead of spinning to maxRounds. Distinct from Luciferase-hthxs (that fixed retained-parent FALSE positives; this is a genuine-but-unresolvable TRUE positive). Note: CrossPartitionBalancePhase.execute returns successful() even when it hits maxRounds without converging — consider surfacing non-convergence.
acceptance_criteria: A coarse cell with a fine 2:1 neighbor whose entities don't span child octants is either refined geometrically to satisfy 2:1, or the loop recognizes it as unresolvable and converges (does not burn maxRounds); bunny demo reaches a stable terminal state without spinning to the cap.
close_reason: 2:1 balance now FULLY converges. subdivide(Key) (the on-demand 2:1 primitive) forces a geometric one-level refine even when all entities map to a single child octant — the load-balancing decline-to-split no longer blocks 2:1, since the constraint is geometric (the finer child cell must exist). Octree+Tetree honour a forceGeometric hook; auto-balance/insert keep load-balancing semantics (unforced 3-arg hook). Result: the real-bunny demo converges 15 violations -> 0 (was pinned at 15, then 4 after hthxs). Stacked review fixed a real traversal bug (empty-internal parents were skipped by visitor traversal), stale docs, dead code, and added the missing forced-subdivide+traversal unit test (verified non-vacuous). Branch feature/hthxs-two-one-balance-leaf-aware, unpushed.

title: 2:1 balance does not converge on a single Octree: checker matches retained internal parents after subdivide (false-positive violations, loop hits maxRounds)
description: Discovered via a real-bunny 2:1 demonstration (portal BunnyTwoOneBalanceDemoTest). Built a coarse level-6 bunny (6812 cells), planted a fine level-8 ghost against a coarse surface cell -> TwoOneBalanceChecker.findViolations correctly detects 15 real 2:1 violations (level 6 vs 8, diff 2, local must refine). CrossPartitionBalancePhase.execute runs and DOES subdivide (finer-than-coarse cells 0 -> 8, ghost re-sync fires, successful), BUT it runs the full maxRounds (10) and a re-scan still reports 15 violations -> NO CONVERGENCE. Root observation: Octree.subdivide RETAINS the coarse cell as an internal parent node (documented in TwoOneBalanceEndToEndTest), and TwoOneBalanceChecker's coarse-band probe matches any stored key at the coarse origin -- including the retained internal parent -- so the boundary keeps reporting a violation even though level-7 leaf children now cover it (diff 1, actually balanced). The 2:1 constraint applies to LEAF elements; matching internal parents is a false positive that blocks convergence (always burns maxRounds). The maintained unit E2E test masks this by driving convergence via a checker seam tied to 'node count grew', not a real re-scan. WHAT: the coarse-band occupancy probe should consider only leaf cells (or subdivide should remove the parent key), so distributed 2:1 balance converges to 0 violations on Octree rather than capping at maxRounds. Verify same on Tetree/Pyramid.
acceptance_criteria: On a single Octree (and Tetree), a planted coarse-vs-fine 2:1 violation is resolved to 0 violations by the real CrossPartitionBalancePhase re-scan (not just refined-then-still-flagged); the checker does not report violations against subdivided internal parents whose leaf children satisfy 2:1; converges in < maxRounds.
close_reason: Leaf-aware 2:1 violation detection across both checker paths. Promoted SpatialIndex.hasChildren(Key) to the interface; the Morton coarse-band probe and the Tetree/Pyramid detector path now skip retained internal parents (subdivided cells whose finer children cover the boundary) instead of re-reporting them forever. Fixed the multi-tree break->continue false-negative. Octree end-to-end convergence proven via a REAL re-scan -> 0 violations (TwoOneBalanceConvergenceTest, no seam); discriminator test covers Octree+Tetree hasChildren; bunny demo on real 47705-voxel geometry detects 15 real violations and the re-scan now drops to 4 as cells refine (was pinned at 15). Stacked review (both reviewers) drove the completion across index types + multi-tree. Residual unrefinable cells (subdivide-refused) are a separate genuine-but-unresolvable gap, tracked separately. Branch feature/hthxs-two-one-balance-leaf-aware (off main), unpushed.

title: gRPC SyncGhosts response amplification + client-side maxInboundMessageSize (DoS follow-up)
description: T8/06ujn review follow-up (RDR-013 deferred). (1) SyncGhosts is unary: a small SyncRequest listing many tree_ids makes the server build an arbitrarily large SyncResponse before sending — the server INBOUND bound does not cap OUTBOUND size. Cap tree_ids count (reject oversized with INVALID_ARGUMENT) and/or bound the response. (2) GhostServiceClient's ManagedChannel sets no maxInboundMessageSize, so the receiving side has no cap on responses. Apply a client-side inbound bound. Neither is a crash today; both are amplification DoS vectors flagged by code-review-expert.
close_reason: Server: MAX_SYNC_TREE_IDS=4096 (INVALID_ARGUMENT fan-out cap) + MAX_RESPONSE_GHOST_ELEMENTS=1M outbound bound checked via getNumGhostElements() before building, on both syncGhosts and requestGhosts (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED). Client: maxInboundMessageSize=4MiB. Stacked review: round1 critic NOT-JUSTIFIED (drove outbound bound); round2 JUSTIFIED/high/0-0. GhostSyncTreeIdCapTest 4/4. PR #206, commit 7ecf8e6f.

title: kNN (FineGrainedLockingStrategy) does not coordinate with the global write lock — reads observe torn state during writes
description: AbstractSpatialIndex.kNearestNeighbors delegates to KnnSearcher which uses core.lockingStrategy().executeRead(nodeIndex, ...) — per-node StampedLocks in FineGrainedLockingStrategy, independent of the global ASI.lock (ReentrantReadWriteLock). But all write paths (single insert/remove via entityLifecycle, and the aqx6x batch fix) take ASI.lock.writeLock(). So a concurrent kNN can traverse the index and observe torn/partial state during ANY write, not just batches. Range queries (entitiesInRegion) and collision (CollisionEngine) correctly take core.lock().readLock(); kNN is the outlier. Discovered during aqx6x stacked review (2026-06-02). Fix options: (a) wrap kNN in ASI.lock.readLock() as an outer guard (simplest, but reduces the fine-grained design's read-during-write concurrency for kNN), or (b) make writes engage the fine-grained strategy so per-node locks coordinate. This is a design decision (RDR-worthy) since it touches the locking architecture.
close_reason: Closed

title: MortonKey.parent() uses >>3 (level-relative) but codes are absolute — wrong parent at level<21; investigate live StackBasedTreeBuilder/AbstractSpatialIndex callers
description: Discovered during Luciferase-3aut. MortonKey stores ABSOLUTE Morton codes (fromCoordinates/calculateMortonIndex quantize world coords then encode; low 3*(21-level) bits are zero). But MortonKey.parent() computes parentCode = mortonCode >> 3, which is the LEVEL-RELATIVE (right-justified) convention. For absolute codes that is wrong at any level < 21. Empirically (jshell): fromCoordinates(2,2,2,L20).parent() = (code=7, L19), but the real coarse cell fromCoordinates(2,2,2,L19) = (code=0, L19); parent()!=real. The correct absolute parent code is mask: mortonCode & ~((1L<<(3*(21-(L-1))))-1). Live callers on MortonKey: StackBasedTreeBuilder.java:183,280 (descending-level build loop, runs for every Octree via AbstractSpatialIndex ctor) and AbstractSpatialIndex.java:2641 (MERGE path). NOTE 2835 lucien tests pass, so either these paths aren't exercised at level<21, or the builder uses a compensating relative convention, or it's a latent bug. ACTION: verify whether parent() output is actually consumed as an absolute key (compare against containsSpatialKey-stored codes) in each caller; if so, fix parent() with masking + add cross-level regression tests; if the builder is internally relative, document the dual convention explicitly. Do NOT assume broken without confirming the consumer convention.
close_reason: Fixed: reimplemented MortonKey.parent()/getChild()/firstDescendantAtLevel()/lastDescendantAtLevel() under the absolute Morton convention (was level-relative, mismatching all stored absolute keys at level<21). Investigation confirmed the bug was dormant on default paths (pointerless SFC, TOP_DOWN build, OctreeBalancer absolute encode); live consumer LCAMovementOptimizer.findLCA now geometrically correct. New MortonKeyHierarchyConventionTest + 2 consumer tests updated. Stacked review passed (code-review-expert + substantive-critic, 0 critical). Suites green: lucien 2840, render 1886, sim compiles.

title: TwoOneBalanceChecker Morton neighbor-find: ancestor-code coarse probe + finer-band enumeration + numTrees-axis routing
description:
kd79 follow-up (substantive-critic SIG-1/SIG-2, 2026-06-01). kd79 delivered the sound level-scan prune (skip |level-ghostLevel|<=1). Three deferred items the critic surfaced in checkMortonNeighborsForViolations:

(1) CORRECTNESS - coarse band: the loop probes new MortonKey(neighborMortonCode, coarseLevel) using the FULL fine code at a coarse level. A real coarse ancestor cell has the SHIFTED code. So coarse-local violations are detected only in the rare cell-aligned case and otherwise MISSED. Fix: for coarse level C, probe MortonKey(neighborMortonCode >>> (3*(ghostLevel - C)), C) (the parent-walk code). This is O(log N) per coarse level and is the bead's intended 'bounded' coarse lookup. Behavioral change (detects previously-missed coarse-local violations) -> needs a deterministic Morton-aligned test (critic recipe: ghostLevel=10, coarseLevel=5, neighbor coord 32-aligned).

(2) CORRECTNESS - finer band [L+2,21]: probes MortonKey(neighborMortonCode, finerLevel), which is not a descendant code, so finer-local violations are also narrowly/incorrectly probed. Genuinely needs descendant enumeration or a code-first secondary index (no key-level primitive under level-first MortonKey ordering; cousin of 701x).

(3) PERF - numTrees axis: the inner 'for tree : forest.getAllTrees()' is O(numTrees) per (level,direction). The bead's floorKey/ceilingKey O(log N) is INFEASIBLE (MortonKey.compareTo level-first gives no spatial containment). A real numTrees-axis bound needs forest-level spatial routing ('which tree owns this key') rather than iterating all trees.

Scope: this is a correctness+perf rework of Morton neighbor-violation detection, separate from kd79's sound level-scan prune. checkDetectorNeighborsForViolations (non-Morton) already documents the local-coarse/local-fine asymmetry.

title: ESVT Bey/Morton index-space inconsistency: CPU converts childOrder, GPU does not + unstable sort + centroid index mismatch
description: Surfaced by d5o9 stacked review (code-review-expert HIGH/MEDIUM-1, substantive-critic SIG-1/SIG-2). PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by d5o9. Concerns: (1) ESVTChildOrder.CHILD_ORDER stores values from TetreeConnectivity.CHILDREN_AT_FACE[type][face], documented as MORTON child indices. (2) CPU ESVTTraversal.java:~210 treats them as BEY and converts Bey->Morton via BEY_NUMBER_TO_INDEX[parentType][beyIdx] before hasChild/getChildIndex (a double-conversion if they are already Morton). (3) GPU shader raycast_esvt.comp uses CHILD_ORDER values DIRECTLY as childmask bit index with NO conversion. So CPU and GPU disagree on the index convention into the (Morton-ordered, per ESVTNodeUnified) childmask: one of them tests the wrong bit when Bey != Morton. (4) ESVTChildOrder.computeChildOrder indexes Bey-numbered CHILD_CENTROIDS[type][k] with Morton child index children[i] -> sort distances use wrong centroids (front-to-back order approximate; perf not correctness). (5) The distance bubble-sort has no tie-break -> non-canonical order if two children are equidistant. RESOLUTION: determine the authoritative index convention of CHILDREN_AT_FACE and the childmask, make CPU and GPU consistent (one conversion policy), fix CHILD_CENTROIDS indexing, add a stable tiebreak, and add an end-to-end CPU-vs-GPU descended-children test (not just order-array parity). d5o9 made GPU order match CPU order (improvement) but left this index-space gap; ESVTChildOrderShaderParityTest guards order only.
close_reason: Co-closed with Luciferase-jk5tk via PR #234. Authoritative ruling: childmask bits and CHILDREN_AT_FACE are MORTON (t8code t8_dtet_face_child_id_by_type port); the CPU's BEY_NUMBER_TO_INDEX conversion was the defect (waft hypothesis inverted — GPU raw use was correct in bit space). All 5 findings resolved by removal: ESVTChildOrder deleted (zero prod consumers after the all-8 rewrite), CHILD_CENTROIDS mis-indexing and sort tiebreak moot, stale BNI docstring fixed, end-to-end per-slot descended-children test added (ESVTPerSlotDescendTest).

title: Owner-range local-interior prune for GhostBoundaryDetector (3uwx S4 deferred perf)
description: 3uwx delivered the partition-boundary correctness contract (flat scan + face-ownership leaf test) and the reusable primitives S1 (SpatialKey.first/lastDescendantAtLevel), S2 (ShapeWeightPartitioner.cutPoints/ownerOf), S3 (SpatialIndex.spatialKeysInRange). The t8code logarithmic-fanout owner-range descent's remaining optimization — pruning local-INTERIOR subtrees to skip the per-element findFaceNeighbors test on elements all of whose neighbors are local — was deferred. WHY: in the single-index-per-rank model the local spatialIndex already holds ONLY local elements, so t8code's remote-subtree prune is structurally already realized (other ranks' elements are absent). The remaining interior prune is sound ONLY with a seam-face check at subtree granularity: a node's neighbor-dilated cube is NOT a single SFC-contiguous range, so it cannot be bounded by ownerOf at the range endpoints alone (an endpoints-only 'entirely remote' prune is UNSOUND — it drops locally-present elements whose SFC position the partition assigns to another rank). Implement the dilated seam-face owner check (per t8code t8_forest_ghost_search_boundary, recurse only into boundary children, face-test at the seam), backed by S1-S3. Perf-only; correctness already shipped in 3uwx.

title: TetreeKey.sfcRangesForKNN under-covers: single range misses entities at non-estimated levels
description: TetreeKey.sfcRangesForKNN returns ONE range from estimateSFCRange (built at a single level chosen by estimateSFCDepth(radius)). But TetreeKey.compareTo is level-FIRST (Compact/ExtendedTetreeKey: Byte.compare(level) before TM-index). So KnnSearcher.performKNNSFCRangePruning's subMap(lower,upper) — both bounds at level L — returns ONLY level-L keys. Entities stored at any other level within the radius sort outside the range and are silently skipped, giving incomplete k-NN results when the SFC-pruning path is taken (maxDistance < MAX_COORD). This is the exact failure MortonKey.sfcRangesForKNN already documents and avoids by emitting one range per distinct occupied level (octree/MortonKey.java:537-555). Fix: mirror MortonKey — collect occupied levels from indexKeys and emit a per-level TetreeKey range (estimateSFCRange needs a level-parameterized variant). Add a regression test: Tetree with entities at mixed levels inside the radius, assert SFC-pruned k-NN == full-scan k-NN. Surfaced during Luciferase-i3e4 (ordering-contract audit).
notes: PR opened (stacked on i3e4 #184). sfcRangesForKNN now emits one range per occupied level via level-parameterized estimateSFCRange; mirrors MortonKey. title: TetreeKey equals/hashCode not uniform across Compact/Extended/Lazy (asymmetric, breaks hash collections)
description: o988 findings (tests in TetreeKeyInvariantTest, @Disabled pointing here): equals is asymmetric across the three TetreeKey impls and hashCode diverges. Root cause: ExtendedTetreeKey extends CompactTetreeKey; each equals() uses instanceof keyed to its OWN class. (1) compact.equals(extended)=true but extended.equals(compact)=false for identical (level,bits) [equalsSymmetry_crossImpl]. (2) lazy.equals(concrete)=true but concrete.equals(lazy)=false (LazyTetreeKey extends ExtendedTetreeKey) [equalsSymmetry_lazyVsConcrete]. (3) LazyTetreeKey.hashCode() returns a Tet-coordinate polynomial, NOT the tmIndex-based hash the concrete keys use, so equal lazy/concrete keys have different hashCodes. All three violate Object.equals/hashCode contract and diverge from compareTo==0 -> unreliable in HashSet/HashMap when impls coexist (GhostZoneManager, TetreeBalancer, TetreeNeighborDetector). FIX: compare equals on (level,lowBits,highBits) uniformly across all impls; align hashCode to the same tuple. AC: remove the two @Disabled markers in TetreeKeyInvariantTest (equalsSymmetry_crossImpl, equalsSymmetry_lazyVsConcrete) and have them pass. Independent of the tkvb encoding flip (pure equals/hashCode contract bug), but tkvb's developer touches all three equals() methods so coordinate to avoid rework.
notes: PR opened. Hoisted equals/hashCode to final base methods over (level,lowBits,highBits); removed asymmetric subclass overrides + lazyHashCode. Both RED tests pass. Full lucien suite 2777/0. Also fixed latent TetreeNeighborDetector self-removal + ExtendedTetreeKey highBits hash collision. Stacked review 0 Crit/0 Sig.

title: render CI flake: cap surefire forkCount to stop OOM-kill of forked JVMs
description: Root cause: root pom test.forks=15 (forkCount=15) applies to render, whose surefire argLine is -Xmx4G -Xms1G per fork. 15 concurrent 4G-capable forks under xvfb+Mesa+LWJGL/FFM native allocations on a ~7GB ubuntu-latest runner over-commit memory. The Linux OOM-killer reaps a fork ('terminated without properly saying goodbye') and the next fork fails to launch ('Error occurred in starting fork'). Non-deterministic; flakes test-other-modules batch (PR #161 observed). The only 4G-needing tests (Phase5a5BenchmarkTest, @Tag memory-intensive) are already CI-excluded. Fix: cap render forkCount via an overridable property; render already overrides argLine so this is the same pattern.

title: RDR-010: Unify Tet/Pyramid element type for cross-shape parent/child/face-neighbor returns
description:
RDR-010 architectural prerequisite for pi1.3 (PyramidIndex). Deferred out of pi1.2 (Finding #14) by design decision 2026-05-29: pi1.2 lands the narrowed, type-system-safe scope (min_tet_level field, separate byte[2][10] pyramid child-type table, computeType returning 6/7, min_tet_level propagation in child()/parent() for the tet-of-tet case) WITHOUT changing any return types. This bead carries the cross-type unification that pi1.2 intentionally excluded.

## Why this exists (the friction)
Knapp 2026 Algorithm 4.1 (parent) and §4.4 (face-neighbor) require that, at the tet<->pyramid boundary, a tetrahedron's parent / face-neighbor may BE a pyramid. Luciferase split the element model into `Tet` (types 0-5, implements Spatial.aabt) and `Pyramid` (types 6-7, NOT a Spatial.aabt per RDR invariant #7). Today:
- `Tet.parent()` returns `Tet` (Tet.java:1691) — cannot return a Pyramid.
- `Tet.faceNeighbor(int)` returns `FaceNeighbor(byte face, Tet tet)` record (Tet.java:1442, record at :2531) — wraps a Tet, cannot hold a pyramid neighbor.
- `Tet.child(int)` returns `Tet` (Tet.java:918) — fine for tet-of-tet (Knapp Alg 4.2b reuses t8_tet_child), but the unified traversal will want a common return.

The pure-Tetree paths never hit this (min_tet_level == -1 always); the boundary only arises inside a PyramidIndex tree, which is pi1.3. So the unification is best designed HERE/against pi1.3's concrete traversal needs, not speculatively in pi1.2.

## Blast radius (measured 2026-05-29, lucien/src/main)
Changing Tet.parent()/child()/faceNeighbor() return types ripples to: ~32 `.parent()` call sites (many explicit `Tet parent = ...` in TetreeFamily, TetreeValidator, Tetree, TetOptimized, TetreeNeighborFinder, TetreeNeighborDetector), ~30 `.child(` callers, 8 `.faceNeighbor(` callers. A covariant-return or common-supertype approach must keep these compiling and behaviorally identical for pure-Tetree.

## Scope
- Introduce a common element abstraction for hybrid tet/pyramid elements (candidate: sealed interface `HybridElement` permitting `Tet`, `Pyramid`, with coordinates()/level()/type()/minTetLevel(); OR make `Pyramid` a `Spatial.aabt` and widen returns to `Spatial.aabt`). Evaluate both in a brainstorming/architecture pass before coding.
- Provide cross-type `parent()` (tet -> pyramid at boundary; Knapp Alg 4.1) and `faceNeighbor()` (types 0,3 -> pyramid along valid face; Knapp §4.4 / Theorem 4.2) returns.
- Keep pure-Tetree call sites compiling and byte-for-byte behaviorally unchanged (guard on min_tet_level == -1).

## REVISES LOCKED RDR INVARIANT #7
RDR-010 invariant #7 states "Spatial.aabt is non-sealed; Tet and aabt.Box implement it; §3b means no new aabt implementor is needed." Unifying the element type may add a new Spatial.aabt implementor (Pyramid) or a new common interface. This bead MUST file an RDR-010 amendment (via /conexus:rdr-research or an RDR Decision addendum) recording the invariant-#7 revision BEFORE implementation, per the locked-contract discipline. Do not silently override.

## Approach gates
- /conexus:brainstorming-gate then /conexus:architecture to choose the unification shape (sealed interface vs widen-to-aabt) against pi1.3's traversal needs.
- /conexus:rdr-research to amend RDR-010 invariant #7.
- TDD; full lucien suite green + -Pperformance parity; /conexus:phase-review-gate.

## Refs
RDR-010 Finding #14, invariant #7; Knapp 2026 Alg 4.1, §4.2-4.4, Thm 4.2 (T2: rdr-010-knapp-geometry-authoritative). t8code origin/main t8_dpyramid_bits.c t8_dpyramid_parent/face_neighbour. pi1.2 narrowing decision: T2 (to be written).

Verified state (2026-05-29):
- Spatial.java:195 — interface aabt extends Spatial (non-sealed; declares containsBound(aabt), intersectsBound(aabt)).
- Tet.java:46 — public class Tet implements Spatial.aabt (not sealed, not final).

title: RDR-010 P5: Forest + balancing integration (N_shape weight hook + TwoOneBalanceChecker shape-router)

Root of the dependency graph. Blocks P2 (connectivity table references pyramid child types), P3 (PyramidIndex stores PyramidKey).

title: RDR-010: Pyramid spatial index (epic)
description:
# RDR-010 Epic: Pyramid Spatial Index

Epic bead for the proposed Pyramid spatial index per RDR-010 (`docs/rdr/RDR-010-pyramid-spatial-index.md`, status `draft` on branch `feature/rdr-pyramid-spatial-index` in worktree `/Users/hal.hildebrand/git/Luciferase-rdr-pyramid`).

## Why this epic exists

Luciferase's three spatial indices (Octree, Tetree, Prism) leave two interlocking gaps:

1. The documented t8code tetrahedral partition gap (~48% gaps / ~32% overlaps in CLAUDE.md / TETREE_T8CODE_PARTITION_ANALYSIS.md).
2. No hex↔tet hybrid transition primitive — practical hybrid meshes (CFD, CAD-to-FEM) cannot be represented.

Published peer-reviewed fix: Knapp/Holke/Spenke/Burstedde/Dreyer 2026 — "A Morton-Type SFC for Pyramid Subdivision and Hybrid AMR" (arXiv:2602.20887v3). Adds pyramid types 6 and 7 alongside existing tet types 0-5, giving exact cube tiling and a published scalable algorithm validated to 131k MPI processes / 40·10^9 elements.

## What lands under this epic (subject to gate)

RDR-010 proposes three candidate directions (A, B, C):

- **A (smallest implementation):** PyramidKey + Pyramid primitive + PyramidIndex + PyramidNeighborDetector.
- **B (recommended end state):** A + Forest weight pluggability (ShapeWeightProvider) so Algorithm 5.1 partitions hybrid forests correctly.
- **C (no implementation):** document Knapp 2026 as the fix in CLAUDE.md, leave gap open.

Phase decomposition is for the gate to decide.

## Hard sequencing constraint

PyramidIndex implementation MUST sequence after RDR-008 closes (god-class decomposition, epic Luciferase-x5i). Current state: P4 (cull extraction) merged via PR #136; P5 (collision extraction) in flight at `feature/Luciferase-x5i.10-collision-extraction`; P6 (entity-lifecycle) still to plan. AbstractSpatialIndex surface is still mutating — coordinate-ordering risk if PyramidIndex lands before P6 close.

**Approach §4 (Forest weight pluggability) has no such constraint** and could start independently — it has value for Octree/Tetree forests even before any pyramid lands.

## Key technical facts to brief implementers

- **PyramidKey** is 128-bit (6 bits/level × 21 levels = 126 bits). Larger than Octree's 64-bit MortonKey, larger than Tetree's compact 64-bit / extended 128-bit. Two-`long` storage likely.
- **`min_tet_level` field** on the `Pyramid` element is MANDATORY for O(1) parent/child/face_neighbor. Without it those are O(level).
- **Tet types 1, 2, 4, 5 are reused unchanged** from Burstedde+Holke 2016 (Luciferase's S1, S2, S4, S5 code paths). Only tet types 0 and 3 get pyramid-aware branches, and only when called from within a pyramidal tree.
- **Forest is already heterogeneous in API** (`addTree(AbstractSpatialIndex<Key, ID, Content>)`) — the missing piece for Algorithm 5.1 is the per-shape `N_shape(ℓ)` weight hook, NOT a homogenization-to-heterogenization rewrite.
- **Pyramid containment primitive** is an OPEN QUESTION: derive a fresh pyramid-DOP, decompose-and-reuse-tet-12-DOP (recommended default), or AABB-then-decompose. Decide at gate.

## References

- T3 catalog: tumblers 1.12.7 (Knapp 2026), 1.12.8 (Burstedde+Holke 2016), 1.12.9 (Holke 2018 PhD), 1.12.10 (p4est 2011), 1.12.11 (t8code v1.0).
- T2 memory: `Luciferase/dt-foundation-papers-indexed-2026-05-28` (resume command for the remaining 14 Tier-3 papers including Holke+Knapp+Burstedde 2019 ghost paper if the epic scope includes distributed pyramid).
- RDR file: `docs/rdr/RDR-010-pyramid-spatial-index.md` (worktree `/Users/hal.hildebrand/git/Luciferase-rdr-pyramid`, branch `feature/rdr-pyramid-spatial-index`).

## Status

NOT CLAIMED. Awaits RDR-010 gate. Do not start implementation phases before RDR-010 status flips from `draft` → `accepted` and RDR-008 P6 closes.

### THE BOUNDED Tetree CHANGE (locked, not free — RDR Structure correction)
Tetree.java overrides the PUBLIC findAllCollisions/findCollisions (lines ~157,169,187,207) with geometry-specific logic that reaches DIRECTLY into spatialIndex, lock, entityManager under lock.readLock(). Once those fields' canonical access is the nucleus/Core, the overrides no longer compile unmodified. Resolution (LOCKED): the facade retains protected access to the nucleus (fields stay protected with Core wrapping, OR protected accessors) — established in P0. P5 refactors Tetree's collision overrides to use that protected re-exposure. Add a Tetree-specific cross-tetrahedra collision test. Without this test the Tetree refactor is unverified. ## RDR-008 G1 — Phase-review-gate (Phase 1: DSOC + Core prep)

Run AT the P1 phase boundary, AFTER P0+P1 work lands, BEFORE P2 starts.

### Gate procedure (all three, in order)
1. `/conexus:phase-review-gate RDR-008 --phase 1` — cross-walk RDR §Approach/§Decision phase-1 scope against the closing P0+P1 beads. Catch silent scope reduction (e.g. a DSOC helper left behind on the facade, a seam not actually wired).
2. `/conexus:review-code` — code-review-expert on the P0+P1 diff.
3. `/conexus:substantive-critique` — substantive-critic on the same diff.
(Steps 2+3 are the MANDATORY review-stacking per MEMORY.md feedback_review-stacking: Luciferase is distributed + security-sensitive; run BOTH at every increment.)

### Pass criteria
- phase-review-gate verdict PASSED (no silent scope reduction).
- Both reviews' actionable findings resolved.
- Full lucien suite (2400+ tests) green.
- -Pperformance parity vs main baseline — DSOC-enabled AND DSOC-disabled configs.
- Auditable: DSOC cluster (state + public API delegators + internal helpers) extracted to DsocController; facade retains only thin delegators. SpatialIndexCore holds the 6-field nucleus; protected re-exposure validated — confirm the partial-bypass risk the RDR Consequences flags is policed (no feature object writes nucleus fields it shouldn't).
- Subclass-untouched: Octree/Tetree/Prism/SFCArrayIndex unchanged (P1-P4 invariant).

Any failure BLOCKS Phase 2. Record gate result in T2 (memory_put project=Luciferase title=rdr-008-phase1-gate.md) — /conexus:rdr-accept-style verification reads gate status from T2.

## RDR-008 P1 — DsocController extraction

Source of truth: docs/rdr/RDR-008 LOCKED Decision item 2, phase 1. Ground against live AbstractSpatialIndex.java (5,851 LOC) — NOT the RDR's 2026-05-25 line numbers.

### Live DSOC inventory (VERIFIED 2026-05-27 via Serena overview + Read)
State (lines 115-132):
- protected `dsocConfig` (DSOCConfiguration) :116
- protected `frameManager` (FrameManager) :117
- protected `visibilityManager` (VisibilityStateManager<ID>) :118
- protected `occlusionCuller` (HierarchicalOcclusionCuller<Key,ID,Content>) :119
- protected `currentViewMatrix` / `currentProjectionMatrix` (float[16]) :121-122  ← camera state, travels with controller
- private volatile perf counters `dsocFrameCount` :125, `dsocTotalTime` :126, `standardFrameCount` :127, `standardTotalTime` :128, `dsocAutoDisabled` :129
- private static constants `MIN_FRAMES_FOR_EVALUATION` :130, `PERFORMANCE_THRESHOLD_MULTIPLIER` :131, `EVALUATION_INTERVAL` :132, plus `MIN_ENTITIES_FOR_DSOC`

Public API (lines 5420-5556): enableDSOC(config,w,h) :5427, enableDSOC(config) :5446, isDSOCEnabled :5453, updateCamera :5460, nextFrame :5480, getCurrentFrame :5490, getDSOCStatistics :5502, getEntitiesNeedingUpdate :5533, resetDSOCStatistics :5543, forceZBufferActivation :5552.

Internal helpers: createIdentityMatrix :5561, frustumCullVisibleWithDSOC :5573, frustumCullVisibleStandard, measureAndExecute, shouldEvaluatePerformance, shouldAutoDisableDSOC, getDSOCOverheadMultiplier, shouldSkipDSOC.

### LIVE DIVERGENCE FROM RDR-008 RESEARCH (changes P1 scope — flag at gate)
1. RDR said DSOC "touches only the lock." FALSE in live: `enableDSOC` (:5437-5438) calls `entityManager.setAutoDynamicsEnabled(true)` + `entityManager.setFrameManager(frameManager)`. DsocController therefore needs the nucleus's `entityManager`, not just `lock` → confirms the P0 dependency is load-bearing, not optional.
2. RDR said "10+ dedicated PRIVATE fields." Several DSOC fields are PROTECTED (dsocConfig, frameManager, visibilityManager, occlusionCuller, currentView/ProjectionMatrix). Before moving them, run `find_referencing_symbols` on each — if a subclass reads them, expose a protected accessor on the facade (delegating to DsocController) so subclasses compile unchanged. If none do (expected — DSOC is generic-only), move freely.
3. `getDSOCStatistics` (:5520) also reads `entityManager.getEntityCount()` — another nucleus touch to route through Core.

### Three seams to wire as callbacks (facade ↔ DsocController)
1. **frustumCullVisible entry** — DSOC early-exit + measureAndExecute(frustumCullVisibleWithDSOC...) vs frustumCullVisibleStandard. The facade's frustumCullVisible delegates the DSOC-vs-standard branch decision to DsocController.
2. **updateEntity visibility/TBV path** — DsocController callback invoked from the facade's updateEntity when DSOC enabled (TBV handling).
3. **node-type selection** — `new OcclusionAwareSpatialNode<>(...)` chosen when DSOC enabled, else the standard node. Facade's node-creation seam asks DsocController which node type to build.

### TDD steps (characterization-first — pin behavior BEFORE moving code)
(i) Write characterization tests pinning CURRENT DSOC-enabled behavior, all RED-against-refactor / GREEN-against-current:
   - frustum cull WITH DSOC vs standard returns identical visible set + ordering (use forceZBufferActivation to exercise the active path)
   - updateEntity TBV/visibility path: moving an entity under DSOC produces same visibility state transitions
   - OcclusionAwareSpatialNode selection: nodes created under DSOC-enabled are OcclusionAware; under disabled are standard
   - getDSOCStatistics returns same keys/values for a fixed scene+camera
   - perf-monitoring auto-disable: drive >EVALUATION_INTERVAL frames at >threshold overhead, assert dsocAutoDisabled flips
(ii) (P0 already introduced full SpatialIndexCore — consume it; do NOT introduce a partial Core here. If P0 somehow deferred, justify and introduce only entityManager+lock access — but P0 is the recommended path.)
(iii) Extract `DsocController<Key,ID,Content>` holding all DSOC state (config, frameManager, visibilityManager, occlusionCuller, camera matrices, perf counters, constants) + the internal helpers. It holds SpatialIndexCore (for entityManager+lock) + the SpatialGeometry<Key> callback IF any helper needs a template hook (verify: DSOC has zero hooks per RDR — confirm frustumCullVisibleWithDSOC's traversal doesn't call a subclass hook; if it does, pass the callback).
(iv) Wire the 3 facade seams to DsocController callbacks.
(v) Keep the public DSOC API ON THE FACADE, each method a thin delegator to DsocController.
(vi) Full lucien suite green + -Pperformance parity (run BOTH DSOC-enabled and DSOC-disabled benchmark configs — the disabled path is the default and must not regress).

### Reminders
- SPAWN parallel subagents: one for characterization-test authoring, one for the perf baseline (enabled+disabled).
- Use sequential-thinking for the callback-vs-direct-reference design at each seam.
- TDD: characterization GREEN on current code first, then refactor keeps them GREEN.
- Update continuation state (memory_put project=Luciferase title=rdr-008-continuation.md) after extraction.
- Subclass-untouched check: re-run `find_referencing_symbols` on each moved field; assert 0 subclass refs OR a protected accessor covers them.
- Context: docs/rdr/RDR-008; scratch d4b358bc-5e98-4b3b-bbee-649215ba6982; existing occlusion pkg (OcclusionAwareSpatialNode, VisibilityStateManager, HierarchicalOcclusionCuller, DSOCConfiguration, FrameManager) is where DSOC machinery already lives — DsocController orchestrates these, does not reimplement them.
acceptance_criteria: DsocController owns all DSOC state + helpers; AbstractSpatialIndex's public DSOC API (enableDSOC x2, isDSOCEnabled, updateCamera, nextFrame, getCurrentFrame, getDSOCStatistics, getEntitiesNeedingUpdate, resetDSOCStatistics, forceZBufferActivation) preserved as thin delegators; 3 seams (frustumCullVisible entry, updateEntity visibility/TBV, OcclusionAwareSpatialNode node-type selection) wired via callbacks; all 4 subclasses compile UNCHANGED; characterization tests pass; full lucien suite green; -Pperformance parity (DSOC enabled AND disabled paths).
notes: FROM P0 STACKED REVIEW (carry into P1): (1) PERF BASELINE — capture a -Pperformance baseline on main (pre-P0 SHA, parent of e2f2ec1b) and store as T2 'performance-baseline-pre-rdr008' BEFORE opening P1's PR, so G1 has a clean two-point comparison (P0 perf parity is by-construction: core constructed once, never read on a hot path). (2) ACCESSOR VISIBILITY + FEATURE-OBJECT PACKAGE — decide where DsocController lives (lucien root vs lucien.occlusion alongside the DSOC machinery); this drives whether SpatialIndexCore's currently-public accessors should be tightened to package-private. If DsocController lands in lucien.occlusion, public accessors are required (or core moves). (3) BYPASS POLICING — P1 reviewer must verify DsocController gets lock/spatialIndex ONLY via core, not a second independent field reference (the partial-bypass risk RDR §Consequences flags). (4) DsocController needs a SpatialGeometry<Key> callback for façade hooks (createNode etc.); P0 deferred SpatialGeometry intentionally.

design:
## RDR-008 P0 — SpatialIndexCore nucleus (prep)

Source of truth: docs/rdr/RDR-008-decompose-abstractspatialindex.md (LOCKED Decision, item 1).

### Why a P0 prep bead (recommendation)
The locked design names SpatialIndexCore (6-field nucleus) + the facade's "retain protected access to the nucleus so subclass overrides keep compiling" as cross-cutting structure that ALL six phases consume. Introducing it incrementally would mean a partial Core grown 6 times (DSOC needs entityManager+lock; k-NN needs knnCache+spatialVersion; entity-lifecycle needs all 6) — repeated edits + repeated review of the same class. P0 establishes the FULL nucleus + the protected re-exposure primitive once, in a no-feature-moved PR with trivially-green tests. This is NOT a new decomposition phase: it moves no cluster and removes no methods from the facade's feature surface. The locked 6 phases (P1-P6) are unchanged.

### Live nucleus fields (verified against AbstractSpatialIndex.java, 5,851 LOC)
- `spatialIndex` (ConcurrentNavigableMap) — :~99
- `lock` (ReentrantReadWriteLock) — :~101
- `spatialVersion` (AtomicLong) — :137
- `knnCache` (KNNCache<Key,ID>) — :138
- `entityManager` — declared near top of field block
- `entityCache` — declared in field block
Note: spatialVersion and knnCache are currently `private final`; entityManager/entityCache/spatialIndex/lock are `protected`. The protected ones are the ones subclass overrides reach (esp. Tetree collision overrides, P5). Re-exposure must preserve at minimum protected visibility of spatialIndex, lock, entityManager.

### TDD steps
1. Characterization: assert current field-access behavior is observable through existing public API only (no new tests of internals needed; rely on full suite as the no-behavior-change pin). Run full lucien suite + -Pperformance on main first to capture the green/parity baseline.
2. Introduce `SpatialIndexCore<Key,ID,Content>` (or non-generic where fields allow) holding references to the 6 nucleus fields. Construct it in AbstractSpatialIndex's constructor from the existing fields.
3. Establish the protected re-exposure pattern: either keep the 6 fields protected on the facade with Core wrapping access, OR add `protected` accessors on the facade. CRITICAL ACCEPTANCE: all 4 subclasses (Octree, Tetree, Prism, SFCArrayIndex) compile UNCHANGED. Run `find_referencing_symbols` on each nucleus field before deciding visibility — Tetree reaches spatialIndex/lock/entityManager directly in its public collision overrides.
4. Do NOT move any feature methods yet. Core is introduced; facade still owns all behavior.
5. Full lucien suite green + -Pperformance parity. Any regression blocks.

### Reminders for the executing agent
- SPAWN parallel subagents for the 4-subclass compile-check and the perf baseline run to conserve context.
- Use `mcp__plugin_conexus_sequential-thinking__sequentialthinking` for the visibility-design decision (protected fields vs accessors).
- TDD discipline: baseline-green BEFORE touching code; the full suite IS the characterization for a no-behavior-change move.
- Update continuation state via memory_put (project=Luciferase, title=rdr-008-continuation.md) after Core lands.
- Context pointers: memory_get(project=luciferase_rdr, title=008-research-1); scratch get d4b358bc-5e98-4b3b-bbee-649215ba6982.
acceptance_criteria: SpatialIndexCore exists holding the 6 nucleus fields (spatialIndex, lock, spatialVersion, knnCache, entityManager, entityCache); AbstractSpatialIndex retains protected access (fields stay protected on facade with Core wrapping, OR facade exposes protected accessors) so all 4 subclass overrides (Octree/Tetree/Prism/SFCArrayIndex) compile unchanged; full lucien suite green; -Pperformance parity vs main.

title: Prism kNN/region completeness for sparse indices (getCellSizeAtLevel int truncation + findNodesIntersectingBounds stub)
description: Discovered during RDR-009 P6 (Luciferase-fok). kNN over a SPARSE Prism index under-returns (k=2 query returns 1) when the nearest entities are several empty cells away. Verified ORTHOGONAL to the S0/S1 diagonal: an all-same-half (all-S0) sparse kNN fails identically, so this is not a two-prism-cover issue. Two coupled root causes, both from the ASI kNN machinery assuming integer coordinate space while Prism uses normalized [0,1) world coords: (1) Prism.getCellSizeAtLevel returns int and truncates the fractional cell size (worldSize/2^level < 1) to 0; performKNNExpandingRadiusSearch seeds searchRadius from it, so the radius starts at 0 and radius*=2 stays 0 -> the expanding-radius fallback (searchKNNInRadius) is a no-op. (2) Prism.findNodesIntersectingBounds(VolumeBounds) is a stub returning empty, so even with a nonzero radius the fallback finds nothing; this also no-ops findCollisionsInRegion (AbstractSpatialIndex:3864) and bounded-spanning search (3979) for Prism.
acceptance_criteria: Sparse Prism kNN returns k neighbors when k entities exist within maxDistance (both same-half and cross-diagonal); findNodesIntersectingBounds returns the actual intersecting nodes over both families; a same-half sparse kNN regression test and a cross-diagonal sparse kNN test both pass. Decide whether to widen the abstract AbstractSpatialIndex.getCellSizeAtLevel int->float (touches Octree/Tetree = ASI contract change; re-weigh RDR-009 Option B) or to override the kNN radius path within Prism.
notes: P6 (Luciferase-fok) intentionally scoped to the diagonal-CROSSING (addNeighboringNodes) and deferred this. The complete fix likely needs AbstractSpatialIndex.getCellSizeAtLevel widened int->float, which is the RDR-009 Option B trigger (changes outside lucien/.../prism) — surface for an Option B re-weigh before implementing.
close_reason: Merged PR #118: Prism sparse-index kNN/region completeness. getCellSizeAtLevel int->float (4 indices); Prism.findNodesIntersectingBounds implemented; gated full-domain kNN sweep (knnRequiresFullDomainSweep, Prism-only). Octree/Tetree behavior unchanged. Full lucien green (2441). Stacked review: 0 critical, comment fixes applied.

title: RDR-005 SPIKE (throwaway): prove forged-cert rejection via KERI verification
description: Load-bearing pre-implementation spike from RDR-005 (must prove before close). Throwaway proof in simulation/src/test that the two-layer mTLS authz model REJECTS a forged cert. Steps: (1) provision a legit Delos ControlledIdentifierMember cert (signed by the member's KERI-committed key); (2) forge a cert = self-signed, DN UID carries the legit member Digest, signed with an ATTACKER key; (3) implement candidate verification (parse member Digest from DN UID -> confirm in Fireflies view/known members -> cryptographically verify cert signature against the member's KERI-committed key from the KERL); (4) assert legit ACCEPTED + forged REJECTED. SETTLES the RDR's open key-material-source question: local KERL public-key lookup keyed by Digest vs verifying the presented cert against the presenter's own committed key. NOT production FirefliesPeerVerifier (deferred to the Inc 7+ distributed wiring); this only retires the security risk. Lives in simulation (where Delos lives). Tracker: Luciferase-va5 (RDR-005).
notes: PROVEN (3/3 green, test-only throwaway): simulation/.../delos/security/ForgedCertRejectionSpikeTest. Verified against delos-0.5.1 sources how a member cert binds to KERI: provision() generates a FRESH ephemeral TLS keypair, the member's KERI signer signs qb64(BasicIdentifier(tlsPublicKey)), and that signature is the DN 'DC' field; 'UID' = base64url(identifier.toIdent()). Member.getMemberIdentifier/getSigningKey are pure DN string parses (no crypto) => forgeable. SETTLES A-vs-B: Answer A. FirefliesPeerVerifier MUST (1) parse claimed Identifier from UID, (2) parse the DC JohnHancock, (3) verify it over qb64(BasicIdentifier(cert.getPublicKey())) against the KERL-COMMITTED key via Verifiers.from(kerl).verifierFor(identifier) — NEVER against key material the cert asserts about itself. Spike shows the forgery is rejected even when the attacker produces a VALID signature over their own key (property = 'must verify against victim committed key', strong form). Naive UID-match accepts the forgery (the vulnerability).
close_reason: Spike proven: ForgedCertRejectionSpikeTest 3/3 green. Settled A-vs-B (Answer A); FirefliesPeerVerifier algorithm recorded (bd remember fireflies-peer-verifier-algorithm). Production verifier is separate work (gated by Luciferase-ah3).

title: Prism full-cube coverage: two-prism design + implementation
description: Address review-360 finding: single Prism index rejects half of [0,worldSize)^3 because a triangular prism only tiles the lower-triangle half-cube. title: IntegrationTest.testConcurrentJoinsHandled NC threshold race-flaky
description:
testConcurrentJoinsHandled at IntegrationTest.java:374 asserts post-concurrent-JOIN neighbor consistency (NC) >= 0.5 for each of 5 concurrently-joining bubbles. Observed deterministic failure at NC=0.43 on Apple M4 Max (5 consecutive runs, identical 0.43 value).

Failure mode: the test acknowledges 'race conditions in neighbor discovery' inline. The 0.5 threshold was set loose enough for CI runners but is undershooted on faster hardware where the race window favors the same eviction pattern.

Confirmed pre-existing — fails on main as well as on feature/luciferase-mj7-tetree-backed-spatial-index without any mj7 changes applied. CI passed on PR #74 / #75 but local M4 Max runs all hit 0.43.

Root cause hypothesis: JoinProtocol concurrent ordering causes some joiners to miss enclosing-neighbor pickups from in-flight peers because findOverlapping is called before peer-N inserts itself. The test acknowledges this race but the threshold doesn't accommodate it on fast hardware.

Fix options:
- Lower threshold to 0.35 with comment explaining the race
- Add @DisabledIfEnvironmentVariable similar to other timing-sensitive tests in this suite
- Make joiner registration in JoinProtocol atomic (acceptor + insert + findOverlapping under a single lock)

Acceptance: testConcurrentJoinsHandled passes deterministically across 100 consecutive runs on M4 Max.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #78 (commit f7413c5a). b3v: test reads context.startTimeMs as deterministic anchor instead of separate wall-clock reading. x0t: JoinProtocol.join() serialised under joinLock to eliminate the concurrent neighbor-discovery race. title: EntityMigrationContextTest.testMigrationContextTimeout is wall-clock flaky
description:
EntityMigrationContextTest.java:343 asserts 'Should timeout at deadline' at startTime+1000ms where startTime is captured BEFORE fsm.transition(MIGRATING_OUT). The transition's internal startTimeMs is captured slightly later than the test's startTime, so when we ask 'isTimedOut(startTime + 1000)' we are evaluating against fsm.startTimeMs + (something < 1000) ms — boundary case under CPU load.

Failure mode observed:
- PR #74 final-suite local run (2026-05-23, hic merge prep): 1 failure
- PR #75 initial CI run (2026-05-23, d8a/jp7): 1 failure on test-batch-3
- Both resolved on rerun without code changes

Root cause: the test uses System.currentTimeMillis() directly, in violation of the project Clock-interface rule (CLAUDE.md §Deterministic Time Handling). The internal fsm.startTimeMs and the test's startTime are sampled at different wall-clock instants.

Fix: inject a Clock into EntityMigrationStateMachine.Configuration (or its FSM); use TestClock in the test so startTime is deterministically equal to the FSM's internal start. The startTime+1000 boundary then becomes exact rather than ±a-few-ms.

Acceptance:
- testMigrationContextTimeout passes deterministically across 100 consecutive local runs
- EntityMigrationStateMachine accepts a Clock via Configuration (or constructor injection)
- Production callers default to Clock.system()
- No new System.currentTimeMillis()/nanoTime() usages introduced in the FSM

Both verified deterministic across 5 consecutive M4 Max runs; 887 broader-suite tests pass.

title: VoN SpatialNeighborIndex.findWithinRadius is O(N) linear scan
description:
In simulation/src/main/java/.../von/SpatialNeighborIndex.java:140, findWithinRadius streams the entire ConcurrentHashMap and filters by Cartesian distance. For N nodes this is O(N) per call, invoked at AoI rate per simulation tick.

The class JavaDoc says it 'replaces Voronoi' but does not use Tetree or any spatial structure — there is no spatial indexing in VoN at all.

Replace with a Tetree (or Octree) instance and delegate to AbstractSpatialIndex.findNeighborsIncludingGhosts(position, radius) or kNearestNeighbors(position, Integer.MAX_VALUE, radius). This is also the natural integration point for any future RD-overlay work.

title: P2.2: Add intersects12DOP() to Tet
description:
Implement intersects12DOP(float exMin, float eyMin, float ezMin, float exMax, float eyMax, float ezMax) on Tet. Tests AABB overlap on all 6 DOP axes: 3 AABB axes + 3 difference axes.

Context: RDR-002, Luciferase-qpv (slab range derivation)
Search keywords: intersects12DOP, AABB intersection, slab overlap, difference axes, 12-DOP

Prerequisites: Luciferase-qpv (slab ranges must be derived)

Execution:
1. TDD: Write Tet12DOPIntersectionTest with known AABB/tet configurations FIRST
   - AABB fully inside tet -> true
   - AABB fully outside tet (AABB-disjoint) -> false
   - AABB fully outside tet (AABB-overlapping but difference-axis-disjoint) -> false
   - AABB touching tet face -> true
   - AABB clipping tet corner -> true
   - Test all 6 S-types
2. Implement intersects12DOP in Tet.java:
   a. AABB overlap check (6 comparisons) — early reject
   b. Project AABB onto each difference axis:
      d_xy: entity range = [exMin-eyMax, exMax-eyMin]
      d_xz: entity range = [exMin-ezMax, exMax-ezMin]
      d_yz: entity range = [eyMin-ezMax, eyMax-ezMin]
   c. For each type, check overlap of entity range with tet slab range (from 2.1) on ALL 3 axes
   d. Return true only if all 6 axes overlap
3. Verify compilation including tests

Key: The tet slab ranges are functions of anchor (x,y,z) and h. They are NOT constants — they shift with anchor.

Parallelization: After this task, Task 2.3 can start. Task 3.1 can also start from Task 2.1.

title: P2.1: Formal derivation of per-type 12-DOP slab ranges
description:
Derive the min/max projection of each S-type's 4 vertices onto ALL 3 difference axes {x-y, x-z, y-z}. The RDR sketch is INCOMPLETE — it checks only 2/3 difference axes per type. This task must derive all 3.

Context: RDR-002, WARNING in RDR about incomplete intersection sketch
Search keywords: 12-DOP slab ranges, difference axes, vertex projection, AABB intersection, permutohedron

Prerequisites: Luciferase-ehl (Phase 1 complete, containment proven)

Execution:
1. Use sequential-thinking for algebraic derivation
2. For each S-type (0-5), get the 4 vertices from Tet.coordinates()
3. Project each vertex onto each difference axis:
   - d_xy = vertex.x - vertex.y
   - d_xz = vertex.x - vertex.z
   - d_yz = vertex.y - vertex.z
4. Record min/max projection for each type × axis combination
5. All vertices share anchor (x,y,z) and h = cellSize. Use relative coords: u=px-x, v=py-y, w=pz-z
6. Express slab ranges in terms of h (or 0): e.g., for S0 d_xy range is [0, h]
7. Produce complete 6×3 table: type -> {d_xy: [min,max], d_xz: [min,max], d_yz: [min,max]}
8. Write results to lucien/doc/12DOP_SLAB_RANGES.md
9. Store derivation in nx memory: project=Luciferase, title=12dop-slab-ranges.md

CRITICAL: The AABB-vs-tet intersection test must check overlap on ALL 3 difference axes, not just 2. Missing one axis produces false positives where an AABB passes the 2 checked axes but violates the unchecked 3rd.

Parallelization: After this task completes, spawn parallel agents for Task 2.2 and Task 3.1.

description:

Context:

  Key files: lucien/src/test/java/.../OctreeVsTetreeBenchmark.java (existing benchmark pattern)

Benchmark design:
- Compare AABT vs AABB range query candidate counts across varying query volumes (1-cell to 1000-cell)
- Compare wall-clock time for both approaches
- Determine crossover point where AABT per-test cost (~40-100 ops) is offset by fewer candidates
- Expected crossover: ~40+ cells per query (speculative, from RDR)

Performance characteristics to measure:
  AABB: 6 comparisons per test, higher false-positive rate
  AABT: ~40-100 ops per test (containment: 4 determinants, intersection: 13 SAT axes), lower false positives

description: registerSyncCallback(Object) at line 372 uses Object parameter instead of GhostSyncCallback interface. Breaks type safety at call site. design:
## Analysis
- registerSyncCallback(Object) at line 372 of DistributedGhostManager.java

- Option B: Keep in balancing.fault, import from ghost (accept cross-layer dep)

## Fix (two parts)
1. Type the parameter: Object → GhostSyncCallback

title: Replace Thread.sleep with proper async coordination in integration tests
description:
Replace Thread.sleep with proper async coordination in integration tests using polling utility:

Problem: Tests use Thread.sleep() for async builds, which is:
- Brittle on slow CI runners (may timeout)
- Wasteful on fast machines (unnecessary delays)
- Non-deterministic (build may not complete in fixed time)

Solution: Add polling test utility with configurable timeout

Implementation:
private void awaitBuilds(int expectedCount, Duration timeout) throws InterruptedException {
    long startMs = System.currentTimeMillis();
    while (builder.getTotalBuilds() < expectedCount) {
        Thread.sleep(50);  // 50ms poll interval
        if (System.currentTimeMillis() - startMs > timeout.toMillis()) {
            fail("Timeout waiting for " + expectedCount + " builds, got: " + builder.getTotalBuilds());
        }
    }
}

Locations to fix (BuildIntegrationTest.java):
- Line 48: testEntityUpdateTriggersScheduleBuild
  Replace: Thread.sleep(100)
  With: awaitBuilds(1, Duration.ofSeconds(2))

- Line 59: testCacheHitSkipsBuild (2 sleeps)
  Replace: Thread.sleep(500) + Thread.sleep(100)
  With: awaitBuilds(1, Duration.ofSeconds(2)) for first build

- Line 91: testDirtyRegionInvalidatesCacheAndRebuilds (2 sleeps)
  Replace: Thread.sleep(500) + Thread.sleep(500)
  With: awaitBuilds(1, ...) then awaitBuilds(2, ...)

- Line 194: testSetBuilder_backfillsDirtyRegions
  Replace: Thread.sleep(500)
  With: awaitBuilds(3, Duration.ofSeconds(2)) or poll queueDepth

Benefits:
- Fail fast on timeout (explicit 2s limit vs arbitrary 500ms)
- Complete immediately when builds finish (avg 50-200ms faster)
- Clear failure messages showing actual vs expected build count

title: Validate ghost layer integration with tetrahedral bounds
description: Verify TetrahedralBounds.toAABB() integration with ghost layer system. Check if Phase 1 tests already cover ghost layer compatibility (TetrahedralBounds.toAABB() tested in Phase 1). If not, add integration tests: (1) Ghost creation after tetrahedral subdivision, (2) Ghost boundary detection with tet-derived AABBs, (3) Cross-tree ghost sync for adjacent tets. Validates that broad-phase culling works with tetrahedral geometry. May already be complete via Phase 1 tests - verify first.
design:
## Ghost Layer Integration Validation

### Objectives
Verify TetrahedralBounds.toAABB() correctly integrates with ghost layer system.
Ensure broad-phase culling works with tetrahedral geometry (AABB wrappers).

### Background
- Ghost layers use AABB-based boundary detection (GhostBoundaryDetector)
- TetrahedralBounds.toAABB() computes bounding box from tet vertices
- Tet AABBs may overlap more than cubic AABBs (S0-S5 tets share edges/vertices)
- Over-detection is benign (extra ghost copies), under-detection is critical bug

### Investigation Phase
**Step 1**: Check if Phase 1 tests already validate this
- Review TetrahedralSubdivisionForestTest for toAABB() coverage
- Check if testTetrahedralBoundsToAABB verifies correctness
- Determine if additional tests needed

### If Additional Tests Needed

**File**: lucien/src/test/java/.../forest/TetrahedralGhostLayerTest.java

**Tests**:

1. **testGhostCreationAfterTetrahedralSubdivision**
   - Setup: AdaptiveForest with TETRAHEDRAL strategy, enable ghost layers
   - Action: Subdivide cubic parent (Case A: 6 children)
   - Verify: All 6 children have ghost layers created
   - Action: Subdivide one tet child (Case B: 8 grandchildren)
   - Verify: All 8 grandchildren have ghost layers created

2. **testGhostBoundaryDetectionWithTetAABB**
   - Setup: Two adjacent S0-S5 tets sharing a face
   - Verify: GhostBoundaryDetector identifies them as neighbors
   - Verify: AABB overlap computed from tet vertices detects adjacency
   - Note: Tet AABBs may extend beyond tet geometry (bounding box property)

3. **testCrossTreeGhostExchangeAtTetBoundary**
   - Setup: Entity positioned exactly on shared tet face
   - Verify: Entity appears in both trees' ghost layers
   - Verify: containsUltraFast() and AABB containment give consistent results

4. **testGhostLayerOverlapWithS0S5Tets**
   - Setup: All 6 S0-S5 tets in one cube (share V0 and V7)
   - Verify: Ghost detection doesn't create spurious copies
   - Verify: Only actual spatial neighbors detected (face/edge adjacency)
   - Note: Vertex-only adjacency (e.g., S0 and S2) should NOT trigger ghosts

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Phase 1 test coverage assessed (may already be complete)
- [ ] If gaps exist, integration tests added and passing
- [ ] Ghost creation works for both 6-child and 8-child subdivision
- [ ] Boundary detection correctly identifies tet neighbors via AABB
- [ ] No false negatives (missing ghosts at actual boundaries)
- [ ] False positives (over-detection) documented as benign
- [ ] No regressions in existing ghost layer tests (simulation module)

title: Optimize BubbleEntityStore reverse lookup with bidirectional mapping
description:
Performance optimization: findOriginalId() is O(n) linear scan, causing O(n*k) complexity in queryRange() and kNearestNeighbors().

File: simulation/src/main/java/.../bubble/BubbleEntityStore.java:255-262

Current Implementation (O(n)):
```java
private String findOriginalId(StringEntityID internalId) {
    for (var entry : idMapping.entrySet()) {  // Linear scan
        if (entry.getValue().equals(internalId)) {
            return entry.getKey();
        }
    }
    return null;
}
```

**Performance Impact Analysis** (10K entities, k=100 neighbors):

**Theoretical (Comparison Count)**:
- Before: O(n*k) = 10,000 × 100 = 1,000,000 comparisons
- After: O(k) = 100 HashMap lookups
- Comparison reduction: 10,000x fewer comparisons

**Measured (Wall-Clock Time)**:
- HashMap lookup has constant overhead (~10-50ns)
- Cache effects, GC, other bottlenecks reduce practical gain
- Expected measured improvement: **10-100x** (not 10,000x)
- Actual gain depends on entity count, k value, hardware

Solution: Add bidirectional mapping (idMapping + reverseMapping).

Implementation:
1. Add reverseMapping: ConcurrentHashMap<StringEntityID, String>
2. Update addEntity() to populate both maps atomically
3. Update removeEntity() to cleanup both maps atomically
4. Change findOriginalId() to reverseMapping.get() - O(1)
5. Ensure thread-safety for concurrent reads/writes

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] reverseMapping maintained in sync with idMapping
- [ ] findOriginalId() is O(1) - verified with HashMap.get() usage
- [ ] **Theoretical**: Comparison count reduces by ≥1000x for n=10K, k=100
- [ ] **Measured**: queryRange() wall-clock time improves by ≥10x for k=100 (benchmark)
- [ ] Benchmark: BubbleEntityStorePerformanceTest measures before/after with n=10K, k=100
- [ ] Memory overhead acceptable (2x maps, ~16 bytes per entity)
- [ ] Thread-safety verified: concurrent addEntity/removeEntity/findOriginalId stress test
- [ ] All existing BubbleEntityStoreTest tests pass

**Why Two Metrics**:
- Theoretical (1000x+) proves algorithmic improvement
- Measured (10x+) validates real-world benefit
- Gap between them reveals implementation quality

References: Code review finding #7 (Important - Performance), BubbleEntityStore.java:255-262

description: Implement LifecycleCoordinator that manages component dependency graph. Kahn's algorithm for topological sort. Start in dependency order (layers 0-5), stop in reverse (5-0). design: Algorithm: Kahns topological sort. Build dependency graph, compute layers (0=no deps), start layers 0->N sequentially (components within layer parallel), stop layers N->0. Timeout: per-component (default 5s), layer-level (max+1s buffer), CompletableFuture.orTimeout(). Concurrency: ConcurrentHashMap, CompletableFuture.allOf() for layers, thread-safe transitions. Test Plan (TDD): testStartOrder, testStopOrder, testTimeoutOnStop, testStartFailure, testIdempotentStart, testConcurrentAccess.
notes: Core orchestration logic. Kahn's algorithm ensures no circular dependencies detected at runtime. CompletableFuture for non-blocking coordination. Thread-safe for concurrent component management. Critical path component. Effort: 8-12 hours.

title: Fix SocketTransport.sendToNeighborAsync returns fake ACK
description: Wraps sync send in CompletableFuture, creates fake ACK without real acknowledgment. Location: SocketTransport.java:189-194. Impact: Misleading API, blocks threads, no backpressure control.
design:
**Fireflies Virtual Synchrony Approach**

Instead of traditional message-level ACKs (message ID correlation, explicit ACK messages), leverage Fireflies virtual synchrony guarantees:

1. Send message via socket
2. Capture current Fireflies view ID
3. Monitor view stability in background (polling every 10ms)
4. If view stable for N ticks (30 ticks = 300ms at 100Hz) → Virtual synchrony guarantees delivery → Complete ACK
5. If view changes (member failure) → Message may be lost → Fail ACK

**Key Benefits**:
- Simpler: No message correlation, no explicit ACK messages
- Stronger guarantees: Virtual synchrony ensures delivery within stable view
- Automatic failure detection: Fireflies handles all failure detection
- 'With high probability' delivery guarantee

**Implementation Strategy** (Polling-Based, Option A):
- Add FirefliesMembershipView and FirefliesViewMonitor to SocketTransport constructor
- Implement awaitViewStability() method (polls view state every 10ms)
- Timeout consideration: Base on Fireflies round timers for normalization

**Files**:
- SocketTransport.java lines 199-204 (replace fake ACK)
- Add constructor parameters for Fireflies integration

**Design Document**: memory-bank:Luciferase_active/fireflies-ack-design.md
notes:
**Approach**: Use Fireflies virtual synchrony for 'with high probability' delivery guarantee.

**Sub-beads**:
- Luciferase-aly0: Design documentation
- Luciferase-00lp: SocketTransport implementation  
- Luciferase-y8gh: Fireflies integration wiring
- Luciferase-1zx4: Test suite
- Luciferase-02a0: Documentation

**Key Decision**: Polling-based approach (Option A from design doc) - simpler than event-driven, minimal overhead (10ms polling for pending ACKs only).

**Timeout**: Consider basing on Fireflies round timers (not fixed wall-clock time) for normalization across different system speeds.

**Pattern**: TRANSPORT_CORRECTNESS_PATTERN.md, Fireflies virtual synchrony guarantees.
close_reason: Fireflies virtual synchrony ACK implementation complete. SocketTransport.sendToNeighborAsync() now uses FirefliesViewMonitor to detect view stability instead of returning fake ACKs. Implementation: Option B (round timer integration), 100Hz tick listeners, 30-tick stability threshold (300ms), 5-second timeout. Fixed RealTimeController ConcurrentModificationException (CopyOnWriteArrayList for thread-safe listener management). All 6 tests passing. Documentation complete in javadoc and CLAUDE.md.

title: Fix flaky test: EntityMigrationStateMachineConcurrencyTest.testConcurrentGetEntitiesInState
description:
## Problem

Concurrency test fails in CI due to race condition:
- **Expected**: Total entities across states <= 101
- **Actual**: Total exceeds 101 during concurrent state transitions
- **Test**: EntityMigrationStateMachineConcurrencyTest.testConcurrentGetEntitiesInState
- **Batch**: test-batch-3

## Evidence

```
[ERROR] EntityMigrationStateMachineConcurrencyTest.testConcurrentGetEntitiesInState:315
org.opentest4j.AssertionFailedError: Total should not exceed 101 ==> expected: <true> but was: <false>
```

CI Run: https://github.com/Hellblazer/Luciferase/actions/runs/21777948439

## Root Cause Analysis

The test creates 100 entities and transitions them between states concurrently. The assertion counts entities across all states:

```java
int total = stateMachine.getEntitiesInState(IDLE).size() +
            stateMachine.getEntitiesInState(MIGRATING).size() +
            stateMachine.getEntitiesInState(COMMITTED).size();
assertTrue(total <= 101, "Total should not exceed 101");
```

**Issue**: The snapshot is **not atomic**. During concurrent transitions, an entity can be:
1. Removed from state A (read returns stale count)
2. Not yet added to state B
3. Total appears to be N-1
4. OR double-counted if reads interleave with adds

Under CI contention, thread scheduling delays exacerbate this race window.

## Solution Options

1. **Atomic snapshot**: Add getStateCounts() method returning atomic snapshot
2. **Relax assertion**: Accept total >= 99 && total <= 102 (±1 tolerance)
3. **Synchronize counting**: Use synchronized block for count aggregation
4. **Redesign test**: Test invariant that doesn't require atomic multi-state read

## Recommended Approach

Option 1 (atomic snapshot):
```java
// In EntityMigrationStateMachine
public record StateCounts(int idle, int migrating, int committed, int total) {}

public StateCounts getStateCounts() {
    synchronized (this) {
        int idle = entitiesInIdle.size();
        int migrating = entitiesInMigrating.size();
        int committed = entitiesInCommitted.size();
        return new StateCounts(idle, migrating, committed, idle + migrating + committed);
    }
}
```

This provides **atomic visibility** of all state counts without changing state machine semantics.

## References

- PR #68: https://github.com/Hellblazer/Luciferase/pull/68
- RecoveryState pattern: Similar atomic snapshot pattern in CrossProcessMigration.getRecoveryState()
- TEST_FRAMEWORK_GUIDE.md: Concurrent test constraints
notes: Implementation complete (commit 3c60ed0c). Added atomic snapshot method (StateCounts record + getStateCounts()) to eliminate race condition. Local validation: 10/10 runs passed. Awaiting CI validation.

- Timing-sensitive test vulnerable to scheduler delays

1. **Relax threshold**: Accept 45+ fps instead of 60 fps in CI
2. **Disable in CI**: Add @DisabledIfEnvironmentVariable for CI=true
3. **Increase test duration**: Run for 2 seconds instead of 1 to smooth out variance
4. **Mock time**: Use TestClock instead of real-time for deterministic testing

## Recommended Approach

Option 3 (increase duration) + Option 1 (relax threshold):
- Run test for 2 seconds
- Accept fps >= 50 (instead of 60) in CI environment
- Maintains test value while accommodating CI variability

## References

- PR #68: https://github.com/Hellblazer/Luciferase/pull/68
