design:
### buildVersion silently truncated from long to int in binary wire format
- Location (verifier-confirmed): **sim:viz/render/protocol/BinaryFrameCodec.java:65, 107, 212**
- Category: serialization · unit=render · flagged by expert
- Root cause: buildVersion is a long in BuiltRegion and BuiltKeyedRegion (monotonically incrementing counters), but it is cast to int before writing to the wire: buffer.putInt(16, (int) region.buildVersion()). After approximately 2.1 billion builds the value wraps, causing clients to perceive builds as older than they are and miss updates. The client-side FrameHeader also decodes it as int, so the mismatch is symmetric — but it is a latent counter wrap bug that becomes observable under heavy traffic. Additionally no comment documents the intentional truncation, making it a silent schema trap.
- Fix: Either (a) extend the wire format header by 4 bytes at byte 16 to carry a full long (preferred, but requires protocol version bump), or (b) document the truncation explicitly and use Integer.compareUnsigned for version comparison to make wrap-around predictable. Add an assertion log.warn if buildVersion > Integer.MAX_VALUE.
- Verifier evidence: The defect is confirmed. In BinaryFrameCodec.java lines 65, 107, and 212, `(int) region.buildVersion()` casts a `long` to `int` before `putInt`. The `BuiltRegion` and `BuiltKeyedRegion` records (RegionBuilder.java lines 604/612 and 484/488) declare `buildVersion` as `long`. The wire format header comment at lines 26-35 allocates only 4 bytes for the field, and `FrameHeader` (line 262-269) decodes it as `int buildVersion`. The truncation is theref

**Build/verify**: `mvn test -pl simulation -Dtest=<NewTest> -Dsurefire.rerunFailingTestsCount=0` (assertions ON).

title: Tetree SFC range pruning is approximate intra-level (min/max-corner tmIndex range not SFC-contiguous)
description: TetreeKey.estimateSFCRange(center,radius,level) builds a range [minCornerTet.tmIndex, getNextKey(maxCornerTet.tmIndex)) at a level. Unlike Morton's bit-interleaved code, the tetrahedral tm-index is an upward Bey-refinement path encoding (CID_TYPE_TO_PARENTTYPE), so it is NOT geometrically monotone within a level: cells inside the AABB can have tm-index values outside the [min-corner, max-corner] interval. The single-level range therefore can UNDER-cover the AABB even after Luciferase-6gnb fixed the cross-level (level-first) under-coverage. Consequence: SFC-pruned k-NN is not exactly equal to full-scan k-NN; KnnSearcher's expanding-radius fallback (fires when candidates<k) masks this for small result sets but not when the estimated-level range returns >=k farther entities. This is a pre-existing limitation of estimateSFCRange, independent of and not fixed by 6gnb. Possible fixes: LITMAX/BIGMIN-style range decomposition for the tetrahedral SFC, or multiple sub-ranges per level covering the AABB cells. Surfaced during Luciferase-6gnb review (both reviewers confirmed the intra-level non-contiguity). Low priority: the expanding-radius fallback provides a correctness safety net for typical k-NN; impact is degraded pruning precision/recall, not silently wrong results in the common case.
notes: INVESTIGATION 2026-06-02 (deferred by user). Confirmed root cause in TetreeKey.estimateSFCRange (L453): range is [minCornerTet.tmIndex, getNextKey(maxCornerTet.tmIndex)) from only the two AABB corners; tm-index is an upward Bey-path encoding, NOT spatially monotone within a level, so interior AABB cells can sort outside the corner interval -> under-coverage. Exact manifestation in KnnSearcher.knn (L177-183): performKNNSFCRangePruning then 'if candidates.size()<k -> expanding fallback'. Hole: when pruning returns >=k entities that are all FARTHER than a missed closer entity, the fallback never fires -> silently approximate k-NN. sfcRangesForKNN (TetreeKey L553) already issues one corner-range per occupied level; estimateSFCRange(single) is only used by tests otherwise. FIX OPTIONS evaluated: (A) enumerate-all-AABB-tet-cells per level then merge contiguous tm-index runs = EXACT but CATASTROPHIC perf cliff when occupied level much finer than radius (cells ~ (radius/cellSize)^3 -> billions at fine levels); not viable without a cap. (B) tet LITMAX/BIGMIN range decomposition over the non-monotone curve = proper fix, likely research-level. (C) verification pass: after pruning yields >=k, verify the k-th-distance ball is fully covered, else sound fallback = bounded cost, keeps fast path, but needs a confirmed SOUND bounded search (check whether Tetree spatialRangeQuery/findNodesIntersectingBounds is itself corner-SFC-based or genuinely spatial before relying on it). RECOMMEND option C if/when this is prioritized. Existing expanding-radius fallback is the current safety net (covers small result sets).

title: AdaptiveForest.removeTree must emit ForestEvent.TreeRemoved (handleTreeRemoved is dead-letter; standalone removal leaks server assignment)
description: Symmetric gap surfaced by Luciferase-l4p0 (code-review MED-1). DESIGN NUANCE: mergeTrees calls removeTree on its sources — if removeTree emits unconditionally, a merge would double-announce source removal (TreeRemoved x2 + TreesMerged). Decide whether to (a) emit TreeRemoved only for standalone removals (pass a flag / add an internal non-emitting removeTreeInternal used by mergeTrees), or (b) accept the redundancy (handleTreesMerged source-removal is idempotent). Add a test asserting standalone removeTree clears the bridge assignment. Refs: rdr-010-l4p0 review; mirrors the l4p0 TreesMerged fix.

title: RDR-010: element-level + geometrically-filtered PyramidIndex spanning coverage
description: Follow-on from Luciferase-7eb (substantive-critic, 3 significant characterization findings). 7eb insertWithSpanning is CUBE-GRANULAR + conservative, not element-granular: (1) Under-coverage: registers ONE element per cube cell (the one containing the cell centre via calculateSpatialIndex); other pyramid/tet elements in the same cube the entity overlaps are NOT registered (Tetree is element-level; this is weaker). (2) Over-inclusion: no per-cell geometric filter (Octree uses bounds.intersectsCube); every cube origin in the clamped AABB is registered, a conservative superset (possible false-positive range membership). (3) Mixed-level keys: a cell centre in a tet sub-region makes calculateSpatialIndex return a shallower-level key, so the entity is registered at coarser granularity for that cell, and level-specific enumeration will not see those shallower keys. This bead: add a per-cube geometric intersection pre-filter (Octree parity) plus enumerate all pyramid/tet elements per intersected cube and test each against the bounds (Tetree-style element-level coverage), ideally via elementFromKey for level-consistent registration. Tests: element-level findability at both bound ends, tet-straddling mixed-level bounds, removal of a multi-level-keyed span. Refs: rdr-010-3y1-7eb code/substantive reviews; PyramidIndex.insertWithSpanning javadoc documents the current cube-granular limitation.
close_reason: Implemented element-level spanning: insertWithSpanning now descends the pyramid SFC and registers the entity in EVERY leaf whose cube intersects the bounds (collectSpanningLeaves), replacing the cube-granular centre-only registration (item-1 under-coverage). item-2 (over-inclusion) was a non-issue for AABB bounds; item-3 (mixed-level keys) is inherent. Sound (cube-prune never under-covers; cube-conservative per element = over-cover OK, insert/query consistent, no false negatives). Stacked review (code-review-expert + substantive-critic, 0 critical): fixed level-0 crash, post-descent element cap, and added the intra-cube isolating test (single-cube bounds -> span>1). lucien 2858 green.

title: PyramidIndex: implement insertWithSpanning (multi-node entity spanning)
description: RDR-010 pi1.3 deferred: PyramidIndex inherits AbstractSpatialIndex's single-node insertWithSpanning default, so an entity with bounds spanning multiple pyramid nodes is stored at one node only (getEntitySpanCount==1). Octree/Tetree override insertWithSpanning to distribute across intersecting nodes; Prism (the most recent peer index, RDR-009) ALSO inherits the single-node default — so pyramid is at parity with the latest peer, and this is an optional cross-index feature, not a pi1.3 contract gap. Implement a pyramid insertWithSpanning override (distribute the entity to all PyramidKeys whose surrounding-cube/geometry the bounds intersect, via findNodesIntersectingBounds) so getEntitySpanCount>1 for space-spanning bounds, then add PyramidIndex to the shared spanning tests. title: Hoist estimateSFCRange to SpatialKey interface — eliminate instanceof dispatch in KnnSearcher
description:
RDR-008 P3-main follow-up. KnnSearcher.performKNNSFCRangePruning currently does 'instanceof MortonKey / TetreeKey' to route to subclass-specific SFC range estimators (MortonKey.estimateSFCRange, TetreeKey.estimateSFCRange). This introduces cross-package coupling from lucien.cache to lucien.octree and lucien.tetree.

Proposed change: hoist estimateSFCRange(Point3f center, float radius) to SpatialKey<Key> interface (or a narrower SfcRangeEstimator<Key> sub-interface), with MortonKey/TetreeKey/Prism keys providing concrete impls. KnnSearcher becomes oblivious to concrete key subtypes. The MortonKey path needs level-aware overload signature (multi-level submap iteration over distinct storage levels), so the interface needs to handle both single-call (Tetree) and per-level (Morton) shapes — likely returning Iterable<SfcRange<Key>> with single-element Iterable for the Tetree case.

Pre-existing coupling before P3 (lived in the façade), made visible at the package seam by RDR-008 P3-main. Not a P3-main blocker; substantive-critic flagged as Observation 1. Separable refactor.

Acceptance: remove the two concrete-key imports from KnnSearcher.java, remove the instanceof dispatch in performKNNSFCRangePruning, full lucien suite green + -Pperformance parity (this is on the hot k-NN path).
close_reason: estimateSFCRange hoisted to SpatialKey.sfcRangesForKNN via PR #142, squash-merged as 1f684a39. KnnSearcher's instanceof MortonKey/TetreeKey dispatch eliminated; replaced with rootKey.sfcRangesForKNN(...) interface call. MortonKey + TetreeKey + LinkedHashSet imports removed from lucien.cache. Suite 2448/0/0; +122/-97 across 4 files.

title: Invert GhostBoundaryDetector + DistributedGhostManager off concrete AbstractSpatialIndex (RDR-008 P2 follow-up)

title: DSOCPerformanceRegressionTest speedup assertions fail in fast/low-occlusion environments (pre-existing, perf-gated)
description: DSOCPerformanceRegressionTest (@EnabledIfSystemProperty test.performance=true, so NOT run in normal CI/mvn test) has 6-7 failing speedup-ratio assertions when run: testFrustumCullingPerformance ('DSOC should provide significant speedup with heavy occlusion', occludedSpeedup>1.5, :103), testEntityUpdatePerformance ('DSOC should speed up hidden entity updates', hiddenUpdateSpeedup<1.0, :122), testScalingPerformance (:167). Under -Dtest.performance=true: 14/0/0 GREEN (was 7/14 fail). Test is @EnabledIfSystemProperty so doesn't affect default mvn test (2446/0/0 unchanged). title: Exclude perf/benchmark/stress classes from default 'mvn test' (run only under -Pperformance)
description:
ROOT CAUSE behind the recurring flaky-perf-test family (Luciferase-tlb and the a7r/lgu series): the lucien pom binds a surefire 'performance-tests' execution to the default 'test' phase, so plain 'mvn -pl lucien test' runs the 21 *Benchmark classes (e.g. KNNSFCPruningBenchmark ~579s), *PerformanceTest, *StressTest, and Prism*ComparisonTest. This (a) adds ~10min to every local phase-gate suite run ('delaying'), and (b) loads the machine so cold-start/timing-sensitive tests flake ('obscuring' real failures). CI does NOT hit this — CI selects curated test subsets per batch and most perf tests are assumeFalse(isRunningInCI()) / @DisabledIfEnvironmentVariable(CI). So the pain is LOCAL-only, which is exactly where RDR-008 phase gates run their 'full lucien suite green' check.

PROPOSAL: gate the benchmark/stress/perf includes so they run ONLY under -Pperformance / -Pperformance-full (their intended home per CLAUDE.md), not the default test phase. Net: local 'mvn -pl lucien test' becomes fast (~2min) and flake-free; -Pperformance still runs them for real measurement; CI unaffected (it already curates). 

RISK/SCOPE (why this is its own bead, not folded into tlb): touches the intricate lucien surefire config (multiple executions + performance/performance-extract/performance-docs/performance-full profiles) and the performance-metrics extraction workflow (mvn clean verify -Pperformance-full). Needs careful validation that -Pperformance-full still discovers and runs the benchmarks after the default-phase binding is removed, and that no correctness-only test is named *PerformanceTest/*Benchmark. Verify: 'mvn -pl lucien test' runs 0 benchmark classes and finishes fast; 'mvn -pl lucien test -Pperformance' still runs them. Requires user sign-off (build-composition change). Discovered during Luciferase-tlb (RDR-008 P0 window).
notes:
CORRECTION (2026-05-27, verified against root pom.xml): the premise was WRONG. The root pom ALREADY excludes the benchmark/perf family from the default test cycle — surefire <excludes> **/*Benchmark*.java + **/*PerformanceTest.java + **/*PerformanceProfilerTest.java AND <excludedGroups>@Tag('performance'). So a normal 'mvn -pl lucien test' does NOT run benchmarks; there is no ~10min benchmark load and no benchmark-induced flakiness in default phase-gate runs. The earlier 'benchmarks ran under load' observation was an artifact of using '-Dtest=<pattern>', which BYPASSES surefire excludes and pulled the *Benchmark/*PerformanceTest classes back in. OctreeRayPerformanceTest is already excluded from default runs (only ran via the -Dtest bypass), so it never affected phase gates.

RESIDUAL (small): a few perf-asserting tests are NOT caught by the exclude patterns and still run in the default correctness suite, where cold-start can flake them: PrismVsOctreeComparisonTest (*ComparisonTest), TetreeLocateMethodTest (*Test, gated only by assumeFalse(CI)). Luciferase-tlb already ROBUSTIFIED these (warmup+best-of-N), which is arguably BETTER than excluding them since they also carry functional assertions (entity counts, etc.) worth keeping in the default suite. 

RECOMMENDATION: downgraded to P3. Likely CLOSE as superseded by tlb, OR narrow to a hygiene task: add @Tag('performance') to the pure-perf methods that have no functional value in the default suite, leaving the functional+perf hybrids robustified-in-place. No build-composition change to the parent pom is warranted — the exclusion infrastructure already exists and works.

title: Triangle.getCentroidWorldCoordinates returns grid-cell center, not true triangle centroid
description: Triangle.getCentroidWorldCoordinates() (lucien/src/main/java/com/hellblazer/luciferase/lucien/prism/Triangle.java) returns the center of the grid-cell bounding box (x*scale + scale/2, y*scale + scale/2) instead of the centroid of the actual triangle (mean of the 3 vertices). This is the CUBE-vs-TRIANGLE center pitfall (cf. CLAUDE.md: cube center = origin+cellSize/2 vs simplex centroid = average of vertices). After RDR-009 P1 (Luciferase-al5) made Triangle.getVertices() the t8 main-diagonal orientation, the true centroid is: type-0 (lower-right {anchor,+x,+x+y}) = (minX + 2/3*cell, minY + 1/3*cell); type-1 (upper-left {anchor,+y,+x+y}) = (minX + 1/3*cell, minY + 2/3*cell). The cell-center is on the cell diagonal, which is the hypotenuse boundary of both triangles, not their interior centroid.
acceptance_criteria: getCentroidWorldCoordinates() returns the mean of getVertices() (true triangle centroid), correct for both type-0 and type-1; a test asserts centroid == (v0+v1+v2)/3 for both types; PrismKey.getCentroid/estimateDistanceTo consumers (kNN) re-validated green.
notes: Surfaced by code-review-expert during the al5 review (PR #112), flagged as pre-existing (predates P1) and out of al5 scope. IMPACT: PrismKey.getCentroid() (PrismKey.java:227) composes triangle.getCentroidWorldCoordinates() and feeds PrismKey.estimateDistanceTo() — used as the kNN distance heuristic — so the centroid error biases kNN distance estimates. Also used by toString() and PrismGeometry.computeCentroid() (PrismGeometry.java:48). Candidate to fold into RDR-009 P6 query-ops (Luciferase-fok) since it touches kNN, or fix standalone. Relates to epic Luciferase-b3k.
close_reason: Merged PR #124: getCentroidWorldCoordinates now returns the true triangle centroid (mean of getVertices(), type+half aware) instead of the grid-cell center (which sat on the hypotenuse). Fixes the kNN distance heuristic bias (PrismKey.estimateDistanceTo) + PrismGeometry.computeCentroid + toString. Test centroidIsVertexMeanNotCellCenter. Full lucien green (2441).

title: [bug] GrpcGhostChannel.queueGhost TOCTOU race on auto-flush path (pre-existing)
description: Surfaced by RDR-007 PR-B code-review (pre-existing on main; PR-B only git-mv'd the class, body unchanged — verified). GrpcGhostChannel.queueGhost: computeIfAbsent(targetRank,...).add(el) then a separate queuedGhosts.get(targetRank) whose result is dereferenced for the batch-size check. A concurrent flushToTarget (which does queuedGhosts.remove(targetRank) atomically) racing between the add and the get leaves the local 'queue' null -> NPE; also the mutable ArrayList in the ConcurrentHashMap is unsynchronised against a concurrent flush draining it. Fix: per-target lock or ConcurrentLinkedQueue per target; OR if single-threaded by contract, document that on the class. Now lives in lucien-distributed/.../forest/ghost/grpc/GrpcGhostChannel.java after RDR-007 P1.
close_reason: Merged #108. title: Migrate ContentSerializer off com.google.protobuf.ByteString to drop protobuf-java from lucien core
description: Surfaced by RDR-007 PR-B stacked review (both reviewers). lucien-core's ContentSerializer + ContentSerializerRegistry use com.google.protobuf.ByteString in their PUBLIC API (serialize/deserialize), consumed by AbstractSpatialIndex. RDR-007 P1 extracted the gRPC TRANSPORT (clients/netty/proto-message-types) to lucien-distributed but lucien retains a direct protobuf-java dep because of this ByteString contract — so lucien is transport-free but not fully proto-free. RDR-007's 'extract gRPC' framing conflated transport with this serialization coupling. DECISION (record at RDR-007 close): proto serialization in lucien-core is currently ACCEPTED; only transport was extracted. This bead tracks the cleaner long-term: replace ByteString with byte[] (or a lucien-native byte container) in ContentSerializer's public API, adapt NULL_SERIALIZER/STRING_SERIALIZER + lucien-distributed callers, then drop protobuf-java from lucien. Out of RDR-007 P1 scope (would touch AbstractSpatialIndex ctor signature).
notes: Also note (RDR-007 known constraint): io.grpc:grpc-api remains TRANSITIVE in lucien's dependency:tree via common (RDR-005 GrpcAuth helpers) — pre-existing, common-module concern, NOT lucien's transport; out of RDR-007 scope. A separate common-module cleanup could exclude/relocate it if a fully grpc-free lucien tree is desired.
close_reason: Merged #109. ContentSerializer public API ByteString->byte[] (matches SpatialKeySerde); ProtobufConverters bridges at the proto boundary; protobuf-java removed from lucien/pom.xml. title: ButterflyViolationAggregator: hashCode-only violation dedup + missing exchanger null-guard (pre-existing)
description: Surfaced by substantive-critic during RDR-007 Inc3 review (NOT introduced by Inc3 — pre-existing on main; preserved verbatim by the behavior-preserving inversion). ButterflyViolationAggregator.ViolationKey deduplicates violations by (localKey.hashCode(), ghostKey.hashCode()) and its equals() compares only those int hashes — two distinct violations whose keys collide on hashCode would be falsely deduped, silently dropping a real violation. Fix: store the actual SpatialKey objects in ViolationKey and delegate equals/hashCode to Key.equals(). Also (LOW): ButterflyViolationAggregator.exchangeWithPartner uses violationExchanger.apply(...) result without a null guard; the BiFunction contract permits null even though DistributedViolationAggregator's exchanger never returns null. Add Objects.requireNonNull or document the non-null contract. Both are correctness/robustness hardening, orthogonal to the proto-boundary inversion.
notes: Found during Inc3 round-2 stacked review (T2 luciferase/aos-inc3-review-round1-findings + the round-2 review). Low priority — collision probability is low for Morton/Tetree keys and the exchanger is currently always non-null. Also deferred from Inc3: a precise test for the SIG-1 mixed-failure case (real + empty() responses in one round -> reachable ghosts applied, convergence NOT flipped) — convergence is not exposed on BalanceResult, so it needs a test-visible hook; the path is not production-wired until RDR-007 P1.
close_reason: Merged #108. ButterflyViolationAggregator.ViolationKey now stores real keys + delegates equals/hashCode (no more hashCode-collision false-dedup); exchanger null-guard added. ButterflyViolationAggregatorDedupTest 3/3 (ran in CI). Stacked review 0 critical/0 significant.

title: Fix RDG.symmetry table — only 24 distinct images (Luciferase-f2z audit finding)
description:
Luciferase-f2z's parametric audit (PortalCleanupBatchTest.symmetryRdgIsNotYetGroupClosedFinding) discovered that portal/RDG.symmetry() — the RDG-coordinate variant of the 48-element Oh symmetry group — produces only 24 distinct images on a generic point (1,2,3) instead of the expected 48. The verified counterpart symmetryOrtho() correctly produces 48.

The fix requires deriving each of the 48 entries from the verified symmetryOrtho via the toRDG / toCartesian transforms:
  symmetry_rdg(g, p) = toRDG(symmetryOrtho(g, toCartesian(p)))

This is a manual 48-entry math exercise that is out-of-scope for the portal-rdfcc-quality cleanup batch (PR #80). The current test latches the 24-image broken state as a regression anchor so a future fix will hit a failed assertion when correctness is restored, prompting the test update.

Acceptance:
- RDG.symmetry produces 48 distinct images on generic point (1,2,3)
- Parametric closure test for the group operation (compose(g, h) = k for some k)
- Cross-system correspondence: toCartesian(symmetry(g, p)) == symmetryOrtho(g, toCartesian(p)) for all (g, p)
- PortalCleanupBatchTest.symmetryRdgIsNotYetGroupClosedFinding updated to assert 48 (or replaced with the proper closure test)

See: portal/src/test/java/com/hellblazer/luciferase/portal/PortalCleanupBatchTest.java (the latching test)
See: portal/src/main/java/com/hellblazer/luciferase/portal/RDG.java#symmetry (the table to correct)
See: portal/src/main/java/com/hellblazer/luciferase/portal/RDG.java#symmetryOrtho (the verified counterpart to derive from)
close_reason: False positive — root cause investigation showed RDG.symmetry is correct. The original 24-vs-48 finding was a test-point artefact: RDG point (1,2,3) maps to Cartesian (0,1,3) whose 0 component creates a reflection stabiliser (orbit 24, not 48). On a generic-Cartesian-image RDG point (e.g. (1,3,3) → cart (1,2,3)), RDG.symmetry correctly produces the full 48-element Oh orbit. Cross-system correspondence test (symmetry(g,p) == toRDG(symmetryOrtho(g, toCartesian(p)))) passes for all 48 groups and multiple test points: 0 mismatches. PortalCleanupBatchTest now has three group-closure / correspondence tests that confirm the table is correct.

title: SpatialKey.toProtoSpatialKey hardcoded instanceof switch limits extensibility
description:

- a new instanceof branch in this method
- a new field in the .proto definition
- regeneration of gRPC stubs

notes: Design proposal in T2 (luciferase/design-luciferase-546-spatialkey-extensibility). Key finding: instanceof switch is in TWO places (SpatialKey.java:82 AND ProtobufConverters.java:54 — bead description missed the second). Recommend Option D: discriminator + opaque bytes + Java SPI registry. ~2-3 day implementation, 1 PR. Wire-break decision is the load-bearing tradeoff vs Option C (additive bytes extension field, wire-compat dual-path).

title: NeighborDetector.Direction is a 6-Cartesian enum incompatible with tet/oct topology

Currently used only for isBoundaryElement / getBoundaryDirections — Cartesian boundary detection — where it's defensible (domain is Cartesian even if cells are tets). But this enum bakes in a cube-centric assumption that would block:
- A future tet-aware face-neighbor iteration

- A TetOctree's mixed tet(4)/oct(8) face enumeration

Severity: low in current state (boundary detection only). Worth tracking as a forward-compat guardrail before any RD/FCC work.

title: Investigate portal/RDGCS constructor axis init correctness
description:
RDGCS constructor (lines 36-38) does:
  xAxis = toCartesian(X_AXIS.subtract(origin).normalize());

For origin=(0,0,0), this passes (1,0,0) through toCartesian. In RDG the result is (1,-1,0) — length sqrt(2), NOT unit. In Tetrahedral the result is (0, 1/sqrt(2), 1/sqrt(2)) — length 1 by coincidence.

The xAxis field is used in construct() for grid line rendering. In RDG the axis has wrong length. Decide: is the field semantics "RDG axis expressed in Cartesian" (current implementation OK, document it) or "unit Cartesian axis" (current implementation wrong, fix)?
acceptance_criteria: semantics documented; if current behavior matches intent, JavaDoc clarifies; if wrong, fix applied; tests verify

title: portal/Tetrahedral.dot() has multiple incorrect terms
description:
In portal/Tetrahedral.java:99 the dot product against the metric tensor G_ii=1, G_ij=1/2:

Current (buggy):
  return (u.x * (v.x + v.y) + u.y * (v.x + v.x) + u.z * (v.y + v.x)) / 2
       + u.x * v.x + u.y * v.y + u.z * v.x;

Correct (derived from G):
  return (u.x * (v.y + v.z) + u.y * (v.x + v.z) + u.z * (v.x + v.y)) / 2
       + u.x * v.x + u.y * v.y + u.z * v.z;

No production callers outside portal (verified via grep). Blocks lift to lucien.

title: HierarchicalOcclusionCuller.beginFrame races renderOccluder (occluderCount reset / zBuffer.clear vs concurrent occluder render)
description: Surfaced by code-review during Luciferase-b3uz3. beginFrame() calls occluderCount.set(0) + zBuffer.clear()/updateCamera() with no synchronization against concurrent renderOccluder() (DsocController invokes both under a READ lock, so they run concurrently). An occluder rendered into zBuffer just as clear() runs, or an increment racing the set(0), can mis-evaluate the activation threshold for one frame or drop an occluder. b3uz3 fixed the exactly-once ACTIVATION race; this frame-boundary mutation race is the residual. Also note zBuffer.renderOccluder may itself not be safe under concurrent callers. Consider: serialize the occluder/frame critical section (synchronized) or require beginFrame to run under the write lock. DSOC default-off mitigates.

title: ThreadLocalTetreeCache.computeTetreeKey uses LSB-first bit layout, diverges from tmIndex (dead code: useThreadLocalCache never enabled)
description: Surfaced by code-review during Luciferase-lof72. ThreadLocalTetreeCache.computeTetreeKey builds the 128-bit ExtendedTetreeKey via lowBits |= sixBits << (6*i) (i=0 at LSB), whereas Tet.tmIndex uses left-shift-accumulate (i=0 at MSB) -> different/likely-wrong keys for level>1. CURRENTLY DEAD: Tetree.useThreadLocalCache is false by default and has NO setter anywhere (main or test), so the threadlocal branch in calculateSpatialIndex (Tetree.java:1471) and getTetreeKey/computeTetreeKey are never reached. lof72 (drop shallow cache) does NOT make it more reachable -- the branch is still gated by the never-true flag. Recommend: either fix computeTetreeKey to delegate to tet.tmIndex() (simplest, removes the independent re-implementation) OR delete ThreadLocalTetreeCache + the dead branch entirely. Verify with a round-trip test (computeTetreeKey(tet).equals(tet.tmIndex())) before re-enabling.
close_reason: Closed

title: Empty trees accumulate in DynamicForestManager — no reaper, and null-bounds empties never spatially merge
description: Surfaced by substantive-critic during Luciferase-drc6r. A tree created without entities (globalBounds==null, e.g. addTree(...,null) or a post-split tree before first insert) is 'underutilized' but areSpatiallyClose now returns false for it (drc6r NPE guard), so it never merges via the spatial path (it can still merge via the hasNeighbor path). There is NO empty-tree reaper in performAutoManagement — removeTree must be called explicitly. So in scenarios that create bounds-less trees, the forest tree count can grow monotonically. Options: (a) filter entityCount==0 from the underutilized candidate set and add an explicit empty-tree reap pass in performAutoManagement; or (b) decide empty trees are caller-managed and document it. title: [simulation][test] StreamingE2ETest.phaseCAndBFullFlow flaky — 'moved entity should trigger REGION_UPDATE' got null (timing-dependent streaming cycle)
description: Observed flaking on PR #275 CI (test-batch-1), passed on re-run — confirmed flake, unrelated to that PR (portal-only). Failure: StreamingE2ETest.phaseCAndBFullFlow — assertInstanceOf(ServerMessage.RegionUpdate, ...) 'moved entity should trigger REGION_UPDATE via streaming cycle ==> Unexpected null value ... but was: <null>'. A moved entity's REGION_UPDATE did not arrive within the streaming cycle window the test polls — timing-dependent E2E race (the update is produced asynchronously; the assertion samples too early under CI load). Fix: replace the fixed-window/poll-once wait with Awaitility (await until a RegionUpdate is observed, with a generous timeout) rather than asserting immediately after a cycle; or inject a deterministic clock/cycle-pump so the test advances the streaming cycle explicitly before asserting. Location: simulation/.../viz/render/StreamingE2ETest.java phaseCAndBFullFlow. Pre-existing; surfaced during the GPU/test-cleanup sweep.
close_reason: FIXED: StreamingE2ETest.phaseCAndBFullFlow flake. Fix: real build path retained (production retries indefinitely), retry budget 10→40, await 5s→2s, receive 200ms→500ms, getTotalBuildFailures() diagnostic in the assertion (infra-flake vs logic-bug), + documented the BuildQueue.submit re-entrancy invariant. title: [render] ESVT contour PRODUCER: ESVTBuilder emits empty contours — GL contour path (z9qq4) is wired but producer-pending
description:
Found during z9qq4 review (substantive-critic). The ESVT GL contour path is now fully wired (z9qq4: ContourBuffer binding=6 in ESVTComputeRenderer, mirroring the OpenCL path; encoding contract verified — contoursToByteBuffer native-order int stream matches std430 int[], and the shader index arithmetic contourPtr+bitCount(mask&((1<<face)-1)) is byte-identical to the CPU ESVTTraversal reference). BUT no production path emits contour data: ESVTBuilder.build() hard-codes , and ESVTNodeUnified.setContourMask/setContourPtr have no ESVT production call site. So the contour SSBO is ALWAYS the 4-byte placeholder in live renders today — the wiring is correct-but-dead until a producer exists. (The ESVO side, ESVOBuildMode, DOES call setContourMask — use as reference.)

Scope: make ESVTBuilder compute + emit contour data (contour masks per node face + the packed contour int stream encoding normal(18b)+position(7b)+thickness(7b) per raycast_esvt.comp:106-110), populating ESVTData.contours + node contourMask/contourPtr. THEN the z9qq4 wiring + the mesa contour round-trip test (SSBOAccountingGLTest.esvtContourSsboTracksData) exercise it end-to-end, and a value-level GPU render test becomes possible (node with contourMask set → shader reads contours[] instead of early-exiting at contourMask==0).

z9qq4 deliberately wired ahead of the producer (user-approved 2026-06-14). This bead tracks the producer so the dead-until-producer state is explicit, not silent.

title: [render] OctreeGPUMemory + ESVTGPUMemory nodeSSBO have the same ResourceManager size-metadata drift as z2ysz (create-once, glBufferData resize, sizeBytes never updated)
description:
Found by substantive-critic during z2ysz review (verified via resource-1.0.8 bytecode: BufferResource.sizeBytes is final; close() unregister subtracts old sizeBytes, createStorageBuffer register adds new). Same anti-pattern as z2ysz but in the NODE buffers (more impactful — node buffers grow with real octree/ESVT data, the realistic re-upload case; far-pointer tables fixed in z2ysz are usually tiny):
- OctreeGPUMemory.uploadToGPU():155-162 — if (nodeSSBO == null) createStorageBuffer((int)bufferSize); then glBufferData every call. Re-upload with a different nodeCount resizes GL but leaves tracked sizeBytes stale → UnifiedResourceManager.getAllocatedBytesForType(SSBO) under-reports, compounding per resize; budgeting/eviction may over-allocate.
- ESVTGPUMemory uploadToGPU():142-147 — identical.

Fix shape = z2ysz: if (nodeSSBO == null || nodeSSBO.getSizeBytes() != bufferSize) { close old; createStorageBuffer; }.

CONCURRENCY NUANCE (needs review focus, why split from z2ysz): OctreeGPUMemory.uploadToGPU mutates nodeSSBO under the READ lock (lock.readLock()), while dispose() nulls it under the WRITE lock. The existing single create already mutates under read lock; adding close()+recreate frees a GL id a concurrent reader (bindToShader/getBufferId, also under read lock) could hold → stale-id/use-after-free hazard under concurrent upload+render. Either move the recreate under the write lock or confirm uploadToGPU is single-threaded-after-build and document. Verify ESVTGPUMemory's locking too.

Not runtime-verifiable on macOS (GL 4.1; compute needs 4.3) or CI (no GPU) — same limit as z2ysz.
close_reason: NOT-A-BUG (verified) — closed with a mesa-runnable pin test. Suspected the z2ysz size-metadata drift in OctreeGPUMemory/ESVTGPUMemory nodeSSBO, but both classes fix bufferSize/nodeCount as final at construction, allocate nodeBuffer once, and uploadToGPU() re-uploads that same fixed buffer — every glBufferData is the same size, so no drift is possible and the create-once is correct. (z2ysz drift only affects the DATA-driven far-pointer SSBOs whose size varies per upload.) Added GPUMemoryAccountingGLTest (mesa-runnable via ai9tw harness) pinning the invariant: nodeSSBO.getSizeBytes()==nodeCount*8 constant across re-uploads — a tripwire if a resize path is ever added — plus first GL-execution coverage of uploadToGPU. CI-proven: mesa gate executed=4 under llvmpipe 4.5. Also fixed an LWJGL native-extraction race (serialized gl-software run to render.forkCount=1). Merged PR #272.

title: [render][test] DAGOpenCLRendererTest GPU tests testUploadDAGDataToGPU + testRejectNonDAGData broken — call uploadDataBuffers() without initialize()
description:

Fix: add renderer.initialize() before the upload (matching the convention that these tests share a refcounted OpenCLContext singleton).
- testRejectNonDAGData (line ~113): misconceived — wraps a VALID testDAG upload in assertThrows(IllegalArgumentException). The comment says 'create an SVO and try to upload' but the body uploads the valid DAG, so no IAE is ever thrown even with a working context. These pass in CI only because RUN_GPU_TESTS is unset (both skipped). Pre-existing; NOT introduced by ie6v8. Kept out of the ie6v8 PR to keep it focused on device detection.
close_reason: FIXED: 5 broken GPU tests in DAGOpenCLRendererTest, all sharing an init-order bug (uploadDataBuffers — allocates CL buffers — called before initialize(); passed only when a sibling had initialized the shared refcounted OpenCLContext, order-dependent flaky). testUploadDAGDataToGPU + testNvidiaOpenCL + testAmdOpenCL + testIntelOpenCL: initialize() first. testRejectNonDAGData: DELETED (misconceived — assertThrows IAE around a valid upload; the addressing guard is unreachable by type contract — DAGOctreeData.getAddressingMode() defaults ABSOLUTE, no override; not worth a mockito dep — followed substantive-critic over code-reviewer); production guard kept + annotated. title: [render] ResourceManager storage-buffer size metadata diverges after glBufferData resize on re-upload (ComputeShaderRenderer + ESVTComputeRenderer)
description: Found during Luciferase-7stji stacked review (0bn1q), code-review-expert M2. Both ComputeShaderRenderer.uploadData (ESVO far-pointer SSBO) and the 8putk sibling ESVTComputeRenderer create the ResourceManager buffer once at first-call byteCount; subsequent uploadData calls with a different-sized far-pointer table re-orphan the GL allocation via glBufferData (correct on the GL side) but the ResourceManager size metadata is never updated. title: Track RD/FCC / TetOctree spatial-index architectural exploration
description:
Tracking bead for the architectural research thread from 2026-05 session on adding FCC-aligned spatial indexing to lucien.

Considered:
- Phase 1: RD overlay on Tetree (flat, query-time aggregation) — for AoI / radius-ball / k-NN
- Phase 2: TetOctree via Greiner-Grosso refinement — native FCC-aligned hierarchy with octahedron as first-class cell

Math findings (some prior hand-waves corrected):
- An RD contains 48 3-orthoschemes (NOT 24). The 24-tet decomposition mixes orthoschemes with non-orthoscheme pyramid tets of matching volume.
- Parent-RD refinement: 1 interior child RD + 12 face-shared (half-volume each) + 6 four-valent-vertex-shared (1/6 each). NO three-valent-vertex children — those sites have odd parity, not in FCC sublattice. Tet accounting: 24 + 12*12 + 6*4 = 192 ✓.
- 3-orthoscheme Maubach bisection orbit closes in 3 classes (Stevenson 2008); arXiv 2512.07315 (Dec 2025) gives finer 4-class structure with 3-cycle.
- Greiner-Grosso oct refinement: 6 child octs (similar to parent) sharing the parent's center as common vertex + 8 regular tets of edge sqrt(2)/2. Volume conservation exact (8/24 + 6/6 = 4/3 = V_parent).
- RD inradius/circumradius ratio = sqrt(2); cube = sqrt(3); bisected-Kuhn tet ≈ 4.69. RD-overlay AoI speedup over Tetree-direct estimated 2-3× at r=cell-edge, 15-20× at r=8*cell-edge.

Prior art summary: no shipped FCC/RD hierarchical index exists. Three escape camps:
- MSP-tree lattice cycling (Inoue 2008) — fanout 4, no SFC
- Greiner-Grosso tet-oct honeycomb (2000) — proper tree, two cell types
- Cubic super-lattice with RD as overlay (t8code approach) — what Phase 1 would be

Persisted research in nx T3:
- architecture-luciferase-openquestions
- architecture-luciferase-fcc-prior-art (first pass)
- architecture-luciferase-fcc-prior-art-deep (second pass 2020+, Maubach orbit, permutohedral=FCC insight)
- architecture-luciferase-mixedbread-spatial-index-inventory (38-file archive scan)
- architecture-luciferase-tetoct-integration-map (Phase 1/2 hooks + risk assessment)
- architecture-luciferase-portal-rd-audit (50% reusability, 6 bugs identified)
- architecture-luciferase-fcc-mathematical-foundations (rigorous verification + corrections)

Implementation-blocking findings:
- TetreeKey hardcodes 8-way fanout (3 bits/level child index). Phase 2's 14-child Greiner-Grosso oct refinement requires a new key class, not a TetreeKey extension. Real engineering, not 'weeks'.
- Phase 1 surgical hook for RD overlay: portal RD math needs lifting + bug-fixing first (see portal-rdfcc label).
- VoN currently has no spatial index at all (see von-perf label). Switching VoN to Tetree alone would dominate any RD-overlay marginal gain — establish that baseline first.

Decision blocker: explicit Phase 1 go/no-go after VoN baseline is established.
